正統十年進士登科錄

玉音

正統十年三月初六日早，禮部尚書臣胡濙等官於奉天門奏為科舉事：會試天下舉人，選中一百五十名。本年三月十五日殿試，合請讀卷及執事等官少保、禮部尚書兼武英殿大學士楊溥等四十員。其進士出身等第，恭依太祖高皇帝欽定資格：第一甲例取三名，第一名從六品，第二、第三名正七品，賜進士及第；第二甲從七品，賜進士出身；第三甲正八品，賜同進士出身。奉聖旨：「是。欽此。」

讀卷官
光祿大夫、柱國、少保、禮部尚書兼武英殿大學士楊溥，庚辰進士。
資善大夫、吏部尚書王直，甲申進士。
translation_en:
Record of the Metropolitan Graduates of the Tenth Year of the Zhengtong Era [1445]

Imperial Pronouncement

Early on the sixth day of the third month of the tenth year of the Zhengtong era [April 12, 1445], Your Servant Hu Ying 胡濙, Minister of Rites, and other officials submitted a memorial at the Fengtian Gate concerning the civil service examinations: In the Metropolitan Examination of provincial graduates (juren) from across the realm, 150 candidates have been selected. For the Palace Examination to be held on the fifteenth day of the third month of this year [April 21, 1445], it is proper to request forty officials, including Yang Pu 楊溥, Junior Guardian, Minister of Rites, and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall, to serve as Readers of Examination Papers and Functionaries. As for the grades and qualifications of the metropolitan graduates (jinshi), we respectfully follow the standards imperially established by Emperor Taizu, the High Emperor [the Hongwu Emperor]: In the First Class (jia), three candidates are regularly selected; the first-place candidate is accorded rank 6b, and the second- and third-place candidates are accorded rank 7a, all being conferred the title of Jinshi with Honors (jinshi jidi). Those in the Second Class are accorded rank 7b and conferred the title of Graduate of the Jinshi Examination (jinshi chushen). Those in the Third Class are accorded rank 8a and conferred the title of Associate Graduate of the Jinshi Examination (tong jinshi chushen). We received the Imperial Edict: "Approved. Respect this."

Readers of Examination Papers

Yang Pu 楊溥, Grand Preceptor for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Guardian, Minister of Rites, and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall; a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the gengchen year [1400].
Wang Zhi 王直, Grand Master for Assisting toward Goodness and Minister of Personnel; a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the jiashen year [1404].

三月十七日早，文武百官朝服侍班。是日，錦衣衛設鹵簿于丹陛、丹墀內，上御奉天殿，鴻臚寺官傳制唱名。禮部官捧黃榜，鼓樂導引，出長安左門外張掛畢，順天府官用傘盖儀從送狀元歸第。
translation_en:
Sequence of Imperial Honors

In the tenth year of the Zhengtong era (1445), early on the fifteenth day of the third month, the Tribute Scholars (gongshi) proceeded to the Inner Palace for the Palace Examination. His Majesty ascended the Hall of Heaven's Mandate (Fengtian dian) and personally bestowed the policy question.

Early on the seventeenth day of the third month, all civil and military officials attended in court robes, standing in their ranks. On this day, the Embroidered-Uniform Guard (Jinyi wei) set out the Imperial Processional Regalia (lubu) upon the Vermilion Steps and within the Vermilion Courtyard. His Majesty ascended the Hall of Heaven's Mandate, and officials of the Court of State Ceremonial (Honglu si) transmitted the imperial decree and called out the names of the graduates (changming). Officials of the Ministry of Rites carried the Yellow Placard (huangbang), led by drums and music, out through the Left Chang'an Gate and posted it on display. Once this was completed, officials of Shuntian Prefecture escorted the Optimus (zhuangyuan) back to his residence with parasols and a ceremonial retinue.

translation_en:
On the eighteenth day of the third month, a banquet was bestowed at the Ministry of Rites; after the banquet concluded, they proceeded to the Court of State Ceremonial to rehearse the court rituals.
On the nineteenth day of the third month, the Principal Graduate (zhuangyuan) was bestowed court robes, a cap, and a belt, and the metropolitan graduates (jinshi) were bestowed paper money (baochao).
On the twentieth day of the third month, the Principal Graduate led the metropolitan graduates in presenting a memorial to express gratitude for Imperial grace.
On the twenty-first day of the third month, the Principal Graduate led the metropolitan graduates to the Temple of the First Teacher Confucius to perform the ritual offering of vegetables (shicai).
The Ministry of Rites submitted a memorial requesting that the Ministry of Works be ordered to erect a stone stele at the Directorate of Education inscribed with their names.

Zhou Hongmo 周洪謨 [registered in a military household of Changning County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan; Added Student (zengguangsheng) of the County School; specialized in the Classic of History (Shujing); style name Yaozuo; fourth in seniority among brothers; age twenty-six, born on the twenty-third day of the fourth month]: His great-grandfather was Shixiang [Assistant Instructor (xundao) in the Confucian School of Changning Military Prefecture under the Yuan], his grandfather was Benyuan [Assistant Instructor in the Prefectural School of Hejian], his father was Yonglong [Assistant Instructor in the County School of Changyang], and his mother is née Han. His mother is living; his elder brothers are Hongsu, Hongyi, and Hongzhe, and his younger brothers are Hongsheng and Hongfan; he is unmarried. He placed first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 141st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Jun 劉俊 [registered as a commoner of Baoji County, Fengxiang Prefecture, Shaanxi; Student of the County School; specialized in the Record of Rites (Liji); style name Shiying; second in seniority among brothers; age twenty-eight, born on the second day of the first month]: His great-grandfather was Bao, his grandfather was Hongyi, his father is Wei, and his mother is née Su. He placed fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and fifty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Du Zaili 杜再禮; his grandfather was Du Tianli 杜添禮; his father is Du Rongcong 杜榮聰, and his mother is née Yang 楊氏. Both his parents are living. His elder brothers are Du Shenggang 杜勝剛 and Du Shenghai 杜勝海, and his younger brothers are Du Shengneng 杜勝能 and Du Shengquan 杜勝拳. He is married to née Gong 龔氏. He placed thirty-eighth in the Sichuan 四川 Provincial Examination and one hundred thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Lian 陳璉 [registered as a native of Kunshan County 崐山縣, Suzhou Prefecture 蘇州府, Southern Metropolitan Area (Zhili 直隸), under military household status (junji 軍籍); a military student (junsheng 軍生) of the Garrison School of Zhenhai and Taicang Guards 鎮海太倉衞學, specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing 書經); courtesy name Qizhi 器之, second in seniority among brothers, aged twenty-six, born on the tenth day of the tenth month]. His great-grandfather was Chen Junqing 陳均卿; his grandfather was Chen Xianzu 陳顯祖; his father is Chen Jizong 陳繼宗, and his mother is née Lu 魯氏. Both his parents are living. His elder brother is Chen Xuan 陳璿. He is married to née Fei 費氏. He placed sixty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefectural 應天府 Provincial Examination and forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

劉孜，貫江西吉安府萬安縣，民籍，儒士，治《書經》，字顯孜，行三，年三十五，十一月十六日生。曾祖桂平〔元淇州學正〕；祖學隱；父器重，母李氏。慈侍下。兄顯仁、顯愚。娶蕭氏，繼郭氏。江西鄉試第六十五名，會試第一百二名。

translation_en:
Li Liang 李梁, registered in a military household of Xianyou County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a county student who specialized in the Classic of History (Shujing). His courtesy name was Tingjin, he was second in seniority among his brothers, and he was twenty-eight sui, born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Li Tianlin; his grandfather was Li Long; his father was Li Ming, and his mother was née Fang. Both his parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Li Qu, Li Hui, Li Song, Li Chun, and Li [?]. He married née Lin. He ranked twentieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yongxiu 李庸脩, registered in a civilian household of Jishui County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a prefectural student who specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing). His courtesy name was Yongxiu, he was first in seniority among his brothers, and he was thirty-nine sui, born on the eighteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Li Benmeng; his grandfather was Li Zongli; his father was Li Weiqian, and his mother was née Luo. His father was living. His younger brothers were Li Yongli, Li Yongsi, Li Yongkuan, and Li Xinyong. He married née Luo. He ranked first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Zi 劉孜, registered in a civilian household of Wan'an County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a Confucian scholar who specialized in the Classic of History (Shujing). His courtesy name was Xianzi, he was third in seniority among his brothers, and he was thirty-five sui, born on the sixteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Liu Guiping (Subprefectural Confucian School Director of Qizhou under the Yuan); his grandfather was Liu Xueyin; his father was Liu Qizhong, and his mother was née Li. His mother was living. His elder brothers were Liu Xianren and Liu Xianyu. He married née Xiao, and took née Guo as his second wife. He ranked sixty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and one hundred and second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Yi 林義, registered in a military household of Haiyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a prefectural student who specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu). His courtesy name was Shangzhi, he was first in seniority among his brothers, and he was forty sui, born on the first day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Lin Youzheng; his grandfather was Lin Yonghe; his father was Lin Hongxi, and his mother was née Zheng. His mother was living. His younger brother was Lin Zhi. He married née Xu, and took née Zheng as his second wife. He ranked forty-sixth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Bin 李賓: Registered as a civilian household in Shunyi County, Shuntian Prefecture; a National University Student (guozisheng) specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Tingyong, second in generational order, aged thirty, born on the twenty-seventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Fushou, his grandfather was Renjing, his father is Rong (District Magistrate of Haining County), and his mother is née Lu. Both parents are living (juqing xia); his elder brother is Xian, his younger brothers are Bao and Guan, and he married née Yang. He placed forty-first in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and one hundred and ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shuyu 李叔玉: Registered as a military household in Changle County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian; a County School Student (xianxuesheng) specializing in the Record of Rites (Liji); courtesy name Shuyu, fourth in generational order, aged thirty-eight, born on the fourteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Keguang, his grandfather was Bojing, his father was Yun, his mother was née Jiang, and his stepmother is née He. His mother is living (cishi xia); his elder brother is Mengyu (Instructor in the Dangshan County School), and he married née Chen and remarried née Zhao. He placed forty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and one hundred and thirty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Chun 張春: Registered as a civilian household in Zhending County, Zhending Prefecture, Directly Attached (Zhili); a County School Student specializing in the Classic of Documents (Shujing); courtesy name Shizhong, first in generational order, aged thirty-four, born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yi, his grandfather was Jingzu, his father is Jun, and his mother is née Han. Both parents are living; his younger brothers are Min, Sheng, and Cheng, and he married née Liu. He placed forty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Hai 朱海: Registered as a civilian household in Guiyang County, Chenzhou Subprefecture, Huguang; a National University Student specializing in the Classic of Documents (Shujing); courtesy name Kekuan, second in generational order, aged forty, born on the second day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Gezheng, his grandfather was Wenda, his father was Youfu, and his mother is née Song. His mother is living; his elder brother is Xiao, his younger brother is Han, and he married née He. He placed seventeenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and ninety-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Zhen 王鎮 (native of Jining Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, of commoner registration; National University Student; specialized in the Classic of Poetry [Shijing]; courtesy name Jing'an 景安; third in seniority among brothers; age thirty-nine, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fifth month). His great-grandfather was Wang Yiqing 王以清, his grandfather was Wang Caixing 王財興, his father was Wang Xinzhi 王信之, his mother was née Xu 徐, and his stepmothers were née Li 李 and née Zhang 張. Both his parents are deceased. His elder brothers are Wang Yong 王鏞 and Wang Jian 王鑑, and his younger brother is Wang Rui 王銳. He married née Chen 陳. He placed tenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and one hundred and third in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Ye Mao 葉茂, his grandfather was Ye Ming 葉明, his father was Ye Chun 葉春, his mothers were née Tang 湯 and née Chen 陳, and his stepmother is née Shen 沈. His great-grandfather was Sheng Gao 盛杲, his grandfather was Sheng Zhongshi 盛仲實, his father was Sheng Yuanding 盛原鼎, and his mother was née Zhang 張. Both his parents are deceased. His elder brother is Sheng Wenying 盛文英. He married née Xu 徐. He placed seventy-sixth in the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination and one hundred and thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Cheng 劉珹 (native of Anfu County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, of official registration; Added Student of the Shunyi County School in Shuntian Prefecture; specialized in the Classic of Changes [Yijing]; courtesy name Cixun 次珣; first in seniority among brothers; age thirty-seven, born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth month). His great-grandfather was Liu Leshan 劉樂善 (Prefect of Shaoxing Prefecture), his grandfather is Liu Ruqiu 劉汝裘 (invested with the title of Examining Editor in the Hanlin Academy), his father is Liu Linying 劉麟應 (Senior Compiler in the Hanlin Academy), and his mother is née Zuo 左. He placed sixth in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and one hundred and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Pu Yuanshan (Registrar of Guang'an Prefecture); his grandfather was Pu Huiqian (Magistrate of Xinchang County); his father is Pu Xuan, and his mother is née Sun. Qian Xin 錢昕 (registered in a civilian household of Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Area; an added student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents (Shujing); courtesy name Jingyin; second in seniority among his brothers; aged twenty-two, born on the ninth day of the fourth month). His great-grandfather was Qian Gengsheng; his grandfather was Qian Zhongde; his father is Qian Gongda, and his mother is née Wu. Both his parents are living. His elder brother is Qian Huan, and his younger brother is Qian Sheng. He is married to née Zhao. He placed seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 108th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Liang 金亮 (registered in a civilian household of Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang; a student of the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes (Shijing); courtesy name Keming; fourth in seniority among his brothers; aged twenty-seven, born on the first day of the second month). His great-grandfather was Jin Lianggui; his grandfather was Jin Wenhua; his father is Jin Xian, and his mother is née Hu. Both his parents are living. His elder brothers are Jin Youlin, Jin Youfu, and Jin Youzhi. He is married to née Zhang. He placed thirty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 119th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Hou 陸厚 (registered as of military household status in the Andong Central Tun Guard under the Shanxi Branch Regional Military Commission; a student of the Directorate of Education; specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Wenzai; first in seniority among brothers; twenty-eight years old, born on the third day of the eighth month). His great-grandfather was Lu Gui, his grandfather was Lu Fusan, his father is Lu Xian, and his mother is née Xiong. Both of his parents are living. His younger brothers are Lu Shan, Lu Qian, and Lu Rang. He married née Wang, and remarried née Li. He placed sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Chang 徐昌 (registered as of artisan household status in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the Southern Metropolitan Area (Zhili); a Confucian scholar of Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture; specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu); courtesy name Demao; second in seniority among brothers; twenty-two years old, born on the seventh day of the eighth month). His great-grandfather was Xu Fuyi, his grandfather was Xu Sheng, his father is Xu Dao'an, and his mother is née He. Both of his parents are living. His elder brother is Xu Wang, and his younger brother is Xu Sheng. He married née Ye. He placed fourth in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Xuan 徐瑄 (registered as of military household status in Jiading County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the Southern Metropolitan Area (Zhili); a student of the Directorate of Education; specialized in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Zijing; first in seniority among brothers; thirty-four years old, born on the fourteenth day of the ninth month). His great-grandfather was Xu Tingyu, his grandfather was Xu Gongxing, his father is Xu Maozong, and his mother was née Wang. His father is living. He married née Li. He placed first in the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination and eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bian Rong 卞榮 (registered as of civilian household status in Jiangyin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the Southern Metropolitan Area (Zhili); an additional student of the county Confucian school; specialized in the Classic of Documents (Shujing); courtesy name Huabo; first in seniority among brothers; twenty-seven years old, born on the eighth day of the first month). His great-grandfather was Bian Liangyu, his grandfather is Bian Zhongzhang, his father is Bian Shiji, and his mother is née Zhang. Both of his parents and at least one grandparent are living. His younger brothers are Bian Huazhong and Bian Zhennan. He married née Xu. He placed seventeenth in the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination and one hundred and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳雲鵬〔貫浙江紹興府餘姚縣民籍，儒士，治《禮記》，字翼之，行一，年三十，七月十三日生〕。曾祖維一，祖肅初，父濃，母洪氏，繼母吳氏。具慶下，弟雲翰、雲鶚、雲鳳，娶蘇氏。浙江鄉試第四十五名，會試第十五名。
陳暄〔貫福建興化府莆田縣民籍，縣學生，治《書經》，字體日，行一，年四十四，三月二十一日生〕。曾祖彦章，祖善政，父聰德，母鄭氏，繼母胡氏。慈侍下，弟炯，娶李氏，繼黃氏。福建鄉試第，會試第一百二十九名。
translation_en:
Ying Hao 應顥: Registered in a civilian household of Chun'an County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang; an added student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing), courtesy name Wenming, first in seniority among his brothers, aged twenty-six, born on the thirteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Ying Jiwen, his grandfather was Ying Daotong, his father is Ying Ju, his mother was née Fang, and his stepmothers are née Fang and née Zhou. With father and stepmother both living, he has younger brothers Huan, Tun, Jiong, Rong, and Hui, and is married to née Shao. He placed twenty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninety-third in the Metropolitan Examination.
Liu Chang 劉昌: Registered in a military household of Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Area (Zhili); a student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing), courtesy name Qinmo, second in seniority among his brothers, aged twenty-two, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Liu Zi'an, his grandfather is Liu Dayou, his father is Liu Gongli, and his mother is née Ji. With both grandparents and parents living, he is married to née Yang. He placed first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and second in the Metropolitan Examination.
Chen Yunpeng 陳雲鵬: Registered in a civilian household of Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang; a Confucian scholar (rushi) specializing in the Record of Rites (Liji), courtesy name Yizhi, first in seniority among his brothers, aged thirty, born on the thirteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Chen Weiyi, his grandfather was Chen Suchu, his father is Chen Nong, his mother was née Hong, and his stepmother is née Wu. With father and stepmother both living, he has younger brothers Yunhan, Yun'e, and Yunfeng, and is married to née Su. He placed forty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.
Chen Xuan 陳暄: Registered in a civilian household of Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian; a student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing), courtesy name Tiri, first in seniority among his brothers, aged forty-four, born on the twenty-first day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Chen Yanzhang, his grandfather was Chen Shanzheng, his father was Chen Congde, his mother was née Zheng, and his stepmother is née Hu. With his stepmother living, he has a younger brother Jiong, was married to née Li, and remarried to née Huang. He placed [number omitted][?] in the Fujian Provincial Examination and one hundred twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Shida 許仕達 [registered in a civilian household of She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Area (Zhili); Prefectural Student; specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu); style name Tingzuo; eighth in generational seniority; aged twenty-eight, born on the eleventh day of the ninth month]. His great-grandfather was Yuqing, his grandfather was Zhongda, his father was Deren, his mother was née Song, his stepmother was née Wang, and his birth mother was née Bao. Both parents are living. His elder brother is Shiji, and he is married to née Wang. He placed thirtieth in the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination and seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Fu 王福 [registered in a civilian household of Qingyuan County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi; Directorate Student (guozisheng); specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); style name Zongshan; first in generational seniority; aged forty, born on the nineteenth day of the second month]. His great-grandfather was Zhongwen, his grandfather was Zhidao, his father was Yi, and his mother was née Luo. His mother is living (his father having passed away). His younger brothers are Ziqian and Zirang, and he is married to née Niu. He placed first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and ninety-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Kai 金愷 [registered in a military household of Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Area (Zhili); Additional Student (zengguangsheng) at the Prefectural School; specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); style name Yuanzhi; first in generational seniority; aged twenty-three, born on the twenty-sixth day of the third month]. His great-grandfather was Yanming, his grandfather was Chaozong, his grandmother was née Zhang, his father was Yuan [Assistant Instructor (xundao) in the Confucian School of Fenghua County], and his mother was née Li. Both parents are living. His younger brothers are Ti, Yi, and Yu, and he is married to née Xu. He placed forty-second in the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination and twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Third Tier, ninety-seven candidates: conferred the status of Fellow of the Jinshi (tong jinshi chushen).

Tao Quan 陶銓 [registered in a military household in Jiang Department, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi; Department Student; specialized in the Classic of Documents (Shujing); courtesy name Wenheng; first in seniority among brothers; age thirty-six, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fourth month]: his great-grandfather was Tao Zijing, his grandfather was Tao Boqing, his father was Tao Chun, and his mother was Lady Liang. Both parents are deceased (yonggan xia); his younger brothers are Tao Jian and Tao Zhu; he is married to Lady Li. He placed second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and one hundred and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Chi 許篪 [registered in a civilian household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Area (Zhili); Confucian scholar (rushi); specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Zhongle; second in seniority among brothers; age twenty-four, born on the second day of the ninth month]: his great-grandfather was Xu Kai, his grandfather was Xu Mincai, his father is Xu Gong [Assistant Instructor in the Deqing County Confucian School], and his mother is Lady Wu. Both parents are living (juqing xia); his elder brother is Xu Xun and his younger brother is Xu Shao; he is married to Lady Gao. He placed sixteenth in the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination and eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Gang 沈綱 [registered in a civilian household in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian; Added Student of the Prefectural Confucian School; specialized in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Mengju; first in seniority among brothers; age twenty-eight, born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth month]: his great-grandfather was Shen Rong [Judge of Huichuan Guard], his grandfather is Shen Zhong [Police Chief in Fuqing County], his father is Shen Quan, and his mother is Lady Gan. Both parents and grandparents are living (chongqing xia); his younger brothers are Shen Ji, Shen Jing, Shen Lun, Shen Jin, and Shen Shen; he is married to Lady Sun. He placed second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and fifty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Yu 劉諭 (registered in a civilian household of Jishui County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi; Additional Student of Jizhou in the Metropolitan Area [Zhili]; specialized in the Classic of History [Shujing]; courtesy name Xieli; third in seniority among his brothers; aged thirty-seven, born on the fifteenth day of the seventh month). His great-grandfather was Liu Zhirui; his grandfather was Liu Yongyi; his father is Liu Piwu ( Tutor of the Left or Right in the Princely Establishment of Wei); and his mother is née Huang. Both of his parents are living. His elder brothers are Liu Xun (Instructor in the Yibin County School) and Liu Jie (Assistant Instructor in the Yiyang County School). He married a woman née Dai. He placed twenty-third in the Shuntian Prefectural Examination and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Gong 姚恭 (registered in a military household of Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang; Student of the Directorate of Education; specialized in the Classic of Poetry [Shijing]; courtesy name Yanxun; first in seniority among his brothers; aged thirty-nine, born on the fourteenth day of the first month). His great-grandfather was Yao Junhua; his grandfather was Yao Mingli; his father is Yao Tai; and his mother is née Zhou. Both of his parents are living. His younger brothers are Yao Kuan, Yao Xin, Yao Min, Yao Hui, Yao Yong, and Yao Ang. He married a woman née Zhu, and took as his second wife a woman née Li. He placed eighty-first in the Yingtian Prefectural Examination and fifty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Shishen 林時深 (registered in a civilian household of Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian; Additional Student of the Prefectural School; specialized in the Classic of History [Shujing]; courtesy name Shishen; fifth in seniority among his brothers; aged twenty-eight, born on the thirtieth day of the first month). His great-grandfather was Lin Qi (Assistant Instructor in the Xinghua County School); his grandfather was Lin Long; his father was Lin Ju; and his mother is née Song. His father is deceased and his mother is living. His elder brothers are Lin Shu, Lin Zhu, Lin Luo, and Lin Shi, and his younger brother is Lin Jun. He married a woman née Huang. He placed sixteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Fang 趙訪 (registered in a civilian household of Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang; Student of the County School; specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals [Chunqiu]; courtesy name Zishan; third in seniority among his brothers; aged thirty-six, born on the fifth day of the seventh month). His great-grandfather was Zhao Yuanjie; his grandfather was Zhao Zhongjian; his father was Zhao Xianji; and his mother was née Hu. Both of his parents are deceased. His elder brothers are Zhao Jian and Zhao Lun. He married a woman née Huo. He placed eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and thirty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Zhong 吳中 [registered in a civilian household of Meizhou 眉州, Sichuan 四川; National University Student (guozi sheng); specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Xingzhun 行準; first in his generation; age thirty-three, born on the nineteenth day of the first month]. His great-grandfather was Wu Xingwen 興文, his grandfather was Wu Zezhao 則昭, his father is Wu Wenzheng 文政, and his mother is née Liu 劉氏. Both parents are living (juqing xia). His younger brothers are Wu Sheng 昇, Wu Yu 毓, Wu Jie 節, and Wu Shi 式, and he is married to née Tang 湯氏. Zhou Jian 周鑑 [registered in a civilian household of Macheng County 麻城縣, Huangzhou Prefecture 黃州府, Huguang 湖廣; National University Student; specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu); courtesy name Kongming 孔明; first in his generation; age forty-five, born on the seventh day of the third month]. His great-grandfather was Zhou Shou 受, his grandfather was Zhou Ximeng 希孟, his father is Zhou Zhongkui 仲馗, and his mother is née Luo 羅氏. Both parents are living. His younger brother is Zhou Duo 鐸, and he is married to née Lu 魯氏. He placed thirty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Ce 羅䇿 [registered in a military household of Nanchang County 南昌縣, Nanchang Prefecture 南昌府, Jiangxi 江西; National University Student; specialized in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Yingzhao 應詔; eighth in his generation; age twenty-nine, born on the fourteenth day of the intercalary fifth month]. His great-grandfather was Luo Wenfu 文富, his grandfather was Luo Dehou 德厚, his father is Luo Gongqi 公器, and his mother is née Guo 郭氏. Both parents are living. His elder brothers are Luo Biao 彪, Luo Xiao 虓 [Instructor (jiaoyu) in the Confucian School of Changhua County 昌化縣], and Luo Yan 𦠆 [?], and he is married to née Mao 毛氏. He placed fortieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

楊渙〔貫江西吉安府泰和縣民籍，國子生，治《易經》，字德濟，行一，年四十二，十月十六日生〕。曾祖尚友〔元興國縣主簿〕，祖景雲，父復環，母陳氏。慈侍下，弟德廣，娶劉氏。順天府鄉試第五十九名，會試第一百二十五名。

林長清〔貫福建興化府莆田縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治《詩經》，字長清，行四，年三十七，三月二十五日生〕。曾祖良玉〔元延平府録事〕，祖季〔元建寧府司獄〕，父美，母鄭氏。具慶下，兄肆〔兵部司務〕、瑺、鶚，弟鷲、榮、久、庶、𨞬，娶鄭氏，繼許氏。福建鄉試第四十名，會試第一百四十五名。

王鉉〔貫浙江紹興府上虞縣民籍，縣學生，治《詩經》，字宗器，行四，年三十八，三月初三日生〕。曾祖通甫，祖茂，父處安，母董氏。嚴侍下，兄鎮、銈，娶何氏。浙江鄉試第四十九名，會試第四十三名。

丁璿〔貫陝西西安府乾州武功縣軍籍，國子生，治《禮記》，字大器，行二，年二十七，二月二十四日生〕。曾祖從道，祖真，父鍔，母張氏。具慶下，兄瑛，弟璣、璽，娶魏氏，繼張氏。陝西鄉試第十九名，會試第一百四名。
translation_en:
Yang Huan 楊渙 (native of Taihe County 泰和縣, Ji'an Prefecture 吉安府, Jiangxi 江西, registered under a civilian household; National University Student [Guozisheng]; specialized in the Classic of Changes [Yijing]; courtesy name Deji 德濟; first in seniority among brothers; aged forty-two, born on the sixteenth day of the tenth month). His great-grandfather was Shangyou 尚友 (Assistant Magistrate [Zhubu] of Xingguo County 興國縣 in the Yuan dynasty), his grandfather was Jingyun 景雲, his father was Fuhuan 復環, and his mother is née Chen 陳. His mother is living; he has a younger brother Degang 德廣; he married née Liu 劉. He ranked 59th in the Shuntian Prefectural 順天府 Provincial Examination and 125th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Changqing 林長清 (native of Putian County 莆田縣, Xinghua Prefecture 興化府, Fujian 福建, registered under a civilian household; Added Student [Zengguangsheng] of the County School; specialized in the Classic of Poetry [Shijing]; courtesy name Changqing 長清; fourth in seniority among brothers; aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-fifth day of the third month). His great-grandfather was Liangyu 良玉 (Administrative Clerk [Lushi] of Yanping Prefecture 延平府 in the Yuan dynasty), his grandfather was Ji 季 (Jail Warden [Siyu] of Jianning Prefecture 建寧府 in the Yuan dynasty), his father is Mei 美, and his mother is née Zheng 鄭. Both his parents are living; he has elder brothers Si 肆 (Office Manager [Siwu] in the Ministry of War), Chang 瑺, and E 鶚, and younger brothers Jiu 鷲, Rong 榮, Jiu 久, Shu 庶, and Xu 𨞬; he married née Zheng 鄭, and succeeded by a second wife née Xu 許. He ranked 40th in the Fujian 福建 Provincial Examination and 145th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xuan 王鉉 (native of Shangyu County 上虞縣, Shaoxing Prefecture 紹興府, Zhejiang 浙江, registered under a civilian household; County School Student [Xianxuesheng]; specialized in the Classic of Poetry [Shijing]; courtesy name Zongqi 宗器; fourth in seniority among brothers; aged thirty-eight, born on the third day of the third month). His great-grandfather was Tongfu 通甫, his grandfather was Mao 茂, his father is Chu'an 處安, and his mother was née Dong 董. His father is living; he has elder brothers Zhen 鎮 and Gui 銈; he married née He 何. He ranked 49th in the Zhejiang 浙江 Provincial Examination and 43rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ding Xuan 丁璿 (native of Wugong County 武功縣, Qian Subprefecture 乾州, Xi'an Prefecture 西安府, Shaanxi 陝西, registered under a military household; National University Student [Guozisheng]; specialized in the Record of Rites [Liji]; courtesy name Daqi 大器; second in seniority among brothers; aged twenty-seven, born on the twenty-fourth day of the second month). His great-grandfather was Congdao 從道, his grandfather was Zhen 真, his father is E 鍔, and his mother is née Zhang 張. Both his parents are living; he has an elder brother Ying 瑛, and younger brothers Ji 璣 and Xi 璽; he married née Wei 魏, and succeeded by a second wife née Zhang 張. He ranked 19th in the Shaanxi 陝西 Provincial Examination and 104th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
李友聞〔貫直隸徽州府祁門縣軍籍，縣學增廣生，治《春秋》，字進明，行一，年三十八，八月初一日生〕。曾祖均亮，祖子遜，父思賢，母程氏，繼母馬氏。具慶下，弟煥文、尚文，娶吳氏。應天府鄉試第三十名，會試第一百二十二名。

王允〔貫山東濟南府歷城縣民籍，國子生，治《詩經》，字執中，行一，年三十九，九月三十日生〕。曾祖士賢，祖世英，父雲，母劉氏。慈侍下，弟信，娶邊氏。山東鄉試第七名，會試第一百一十五名。

楊禮和〔貫四川重慶府江津縣民籍，國子生，治《春秋》，字節之，行四，年四十四，十月初一日生〕。曾祖濟甫，祖文壽，父鵬，母吳氏。永感下，兄泰和、均和，娶劉氏。四川鄉試第二十名，會試第二十六名。

陳善〔貫河南汝寧府羅山縣民籍，國子生，治《詩經》，字復初，行三，年四十八，二月二十三日生〕。曾祖文顯，祖祖二，父僧，母陳氏。永感下，兄道明、道真，弟道亨，娶王氏。河南鄉試第二十二名，會試第一百三十三名。
translation_en:
Li Youwen 李友聞, courtesy name Jinming 進明, first in seniority among his brothers, aged thirty-eight, born on the first day of the eighth month, was registered under a military household in Qimen County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the Directly Attached region (Zhili). He was an added student (zengguang sheng) of the county Confucian school, specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu). His great-grandfather was Li Junliang 均亮, his grandfather was Li Zixun 子遜, his father is Li Sixian 思賢, his mother was Madam Cheng 程氏, and his stepmother is Madam Ma 馬氏. Both his father and stepmother are living. He has younger brothers named Huanwen 煥文 and Shangwen 尚文, and is married to Madam Wu 吳氏. He placed thirtieth in the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination and one hundred and twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yun 王允, courtesy name Zhizhong 執中, first in seniority among his brothers, aged thirty-nine, born on the thirtieth day of the ninth month, was registered under a civilian household in Licheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. He was a student of the Directorate of Education (guozisheng), specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing). His great-grandfather was Wang Shixian 士賢, his grandfather was Wang Shiying 世英, his father was Wang Yun 雲, and his mother is Madam Liu 劉氏. His father is deceased and his mother is living. He has a younger brother named Xin 信, and is married to Madam Bian 邊氏. He placed seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and one hundred and fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Lihe 楊禮和, courtesy name Jiezhi 節之, fourth in seniority among his brothers, aged forty-four, born on the first day of the tenth month, was registered under a civilian household in Jiangjin County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. He was a student of the Directorate of Education (guozisheng), specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu). His great-grandfather was Yang Jifu 濟甫, his grandfather was Yang Wenshou 文壽, his father was Yang Peng 鵬, and his mother was Madam Wu 吳氏. Both of his parents are deceased. He has elder brothers named Taihe 泰和 and Junhe 均和, and is married to Madam Liu 劉氏. He placed twentieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Shan 陳善, courtesy name Fuchu 復初, third in seniority among his brothers, aged forty-eight, born on the twenty-third day of the second month, was registered under a civilian household in Luoshan County, Runing Prefecture, Henan. He was a student of the Directorate of Education (guozisheng), specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing). His great-grandfather was Chen Wenxian 文顯, his grandfather was Chen Zu'er 祖二, his father was Chen Seng 僧, and his mother was Madam Chen 陳氏. Both of his parents are deceased. He has elder brothers named Daoming 道明 and Daozhen 道真, a younger brother named Daoheng 道亨, and is married to Madam Wang 王氏. He placed twenty-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and one hundred and thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

趙昂〔貫永清左衛左所軍籍，順天府學軍生，治《詩經》，字伯顒，行一，年二十四，六月初八日生〕。曾祖士達，祖源清〔常山中護衛正千戶〕，父傑〔羽林前衛正千戶〕，母張氏。具慶下。弟昺。娶李氏。順天府鄉試第三十五名，會試第六十四名。

童存德〔貫浙江金華府蘭谿縣民籍，國子生，治《春秋》，字居敬，行一，年三十七，十一月二十一日生〕。曾祖永福，祖律，父寵，母趙氏。具慶下。弟存義、存禮、存誠、存忠、存善。娶趙氏。浙江鄉試第三十二名，會試第六十八名。

translation_en:
Xu Xing 徐行 (registered in a civilian household of Shan County 單縣, Yanzhou Prefecture 兖州府, Shandong 山東; a County School Student specializing in the Record of Rites [Liji]; courtesy name Shunli 順理; third in seniority among his brothers; aged thirty-eight, born on the thirtieth day of the tenth month). His great-grandfather was Xu Xing 興, his grandfather was Xu Youliang 友諒, his father was Xu Lian 璉, and his mother is née Gong 鞏. His mother is living. His elder brothers are Xu Wen 文 and Xu Jin 謹; his younger brothers are Xu Zhong 忠 and Xu Xin 信; he is married to née Wang 王. He placed twelfth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Ang 趙昂 (registered in a military household of the Left Battalion of the Yongqing Left Guard 永清左衛左所; a military student of the Shuntian Prefectural School 順天府學 specializing in the Classic of Poetry [Shijing]; courtesy name Boyong 伯顒; first in seniority among his brothers; aged twenty-four, born on the eighth day of the sixth month). His great-grandfather was Zhao Shida 士達, his grandfather was Zhao Yuanqing 源清 (Battalion Commander of the Changshan Central Escort Guard 常山中護衛), his father is Zhao Jie 傑 (Battalion Commander of the Yulin Front Guard 羽林前衛), and his mother is née Zhang 張. Both of his parents are living. His younger brother is Zhao Bing 昺; he is married to née Li 李. He placed thirty-fifth in the Shuntian Provincial Examination and sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

His younger brothers are Yong and Guan, and he is married to a woman née Deng. He placed sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Xiang 孫祥 [native of Datong County in Datong Prefecture, Shanxi, of military registration; a Military Student of the Datong Right Guard specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Tingrui, third in seniority among his brothers, aged twenty-eight, born on the eleventh day of the first month]. His elder brothers are Zhi and Liang, his younger brother is Qi, and he is married to a woman née Wang. He placed fifteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Kai 曹凱 [native of Yidu County in Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, of military registration; a National University Student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu); courtesy name Zongyuan, third in seniority among his brothers, aged thirty-three, born on the twelfth day of the second month]. His great-grandfather was Bogong, his grandfather was Quan, his father is Li, and his mother is née Sun. Both parents are living. His elder brothers are Bin and Jian, his younger brothers are Yan, Zi, Xian, and Guan, and he is married to a woman née Kong. He placed nineteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and eighty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xuan 王宣 [registered in a civilian household in Changshou County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan; a County School Student; specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Dezhao; first in seniority among his brothers; aged forty-three, born on the tenth day of the sixth month]. His younger brothers are Wang Mengqing, Wang Mengtong, and Wang Mengnan. He married a woman née Ran, and took as his second wife a woman née Xie. He ranked thirty-third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and seventy-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
林廷舉〔貫廣東潮州府海陽縣儒籍，府學增廣生，治《春秋》，字雲鵬，行一，年二十九，三月二十六日生〕。曾祖子華〔元福建行省員外郎〕，祖興祖〔交阯布政司參議〕，父厚〔刑部貴州司郎中〕，母張氏。嚴侍下。弟廷皐、廷鞏、廷準、廷申、廷章、廷節、廷甲。娶張氏。廣東鄉試第二名，會試第十四名。

周璹〔貫江西吉安府吉水縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治《詩經》，字式廉，行三，年二十九，九月二十二日生〕。曾祖士章，祖仁本，父楮敬，母胡氏，繼母易氏。永感下。兄珉、珣，弟珍、瑫、瓛、珂。娶劉氏，繼羅氏。江西鄉試第三十二名，會試第一百十八名。

原傑〔貫山西澤州陽城縣民籍，國子生，治《詩經》，字子英，行三，年二十九，二月十三日生〕。曾祖世吉，祖仲和，父彥明，母吳氏。具慶下。兄瑢〔汝州學訓導〕、璟，弟俊、祺。娶宋氏。山西鄉試第十五名，會試第七十名。

宋璽〔貫陝西西安府咸寧縣民籍，府學增廣生，治《易經》，字廷玉，行五，年二十八，四月十八日生〕。曾祖希曾〔元四川貴州達魯花赤〕，祖學，父輩〔河南歸德州知州〕，母胡氏。具慶下。兄亷〔禮部司務〕、玹〔工部織染所副使〕、琰、琮、瑄。娶張氏。陝西鄉試第十名，會試第一百十九名。
translation_en:
Lin Tingju 林廷舉: Registered in a Confucian household of Haiyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong; an added student (zengguangsheng) of the Prefectural School specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu); courtesy name Yunpeng, first in seniority among his brothers, aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-sixth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Lin Zihua, Vice Director (yuanwailang) in the Fujian Branch Secretariat under the Yuan; his grandfather was Lin Xingzu, Assistant Administration Commissioner (canyi) in the Jiaozhi Provincial Administration Commission; his father is Lin Hou, Director (langzhong) of the Guizhou Bureau in the Ministry of Justice; his mother was née Zhang. His father is living and his mother is deceased. His younger brothers are Tinggao, Tinggong, Tingzhun, Tingshen, Tingzhang, Tingjie, and Tingjia. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed 2nd in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 14th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Shu 周璹: Registered in a civilian household of Jishui County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi; an added student (zengguangsheng) of the County School specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Shilian, third in seniority, aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zhou Shizhang, his grandfather was Zhou Renben, his father was Zhou Chujing [?], his mother was née Hu, and his stepmother was née Yi. Both of his parents are deceased. His elder brothers are Min and Xun, and his younger brothers are Zhen, Tao, Huan, and Ke. He married a woman née Liu, and subsequently married a woman née Luo. He placed 32nd in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 118th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Jie 原傑: Registered in a civilian household of Yangcheng County, Zezhou, Shanxi; a student of the Directorate of Education (guozisheng) specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Ziying, third in seniority, aged twenty-nine, born on the thirteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Yuan Shiji, his grandfather was Yuan Zhonghe, his father is Yuan Yanming, and his mother is née Wu. Both of his parents are living. His elder brothers are Rong, Assistant Instructor (xundao) of the Ruzhou School, and Jing; his younger brothers are Jun and Qi. He married a woman née Song. He placed 15th in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 70th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Xi 宋璽: Registered in a civilian household of Xianning County, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi; an added student (zengguangsheng) of the Prefectural School specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Tingyu, fifth in seniority, aged twenty-eight, born on the eighteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Song Xizeng, Overseer (darughachi) of Guizhou in Sichuan under the Yuan; his grandfather was Song Xue; his father is Song Bei [?], Department Magistrate (zhizhou) of Guide Department in Henan; his mother is née Hu. Both of his parents are living. His elder brothers are Lian, Office Manager (siwu) in the Ministry of Rites; Xuan, Vice Commissioner (fushi) of the Weaving and Dyeing Service in the Ministry of Works; Yan; Cong; and Xuan. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed 10th in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 119th in the Metropolitan Examination.

高閏〔貫遼東盖州衛軍生，浙江紹興府山陰縣人，治《書經》，字居正，行四，年二十九，閏五月十三日生〕。曾祖復亨〔元獻州知州〕；祖宗泗；父貴珦；母王氏。具慶下。兄簡、靖、黙；弟寧、實、勤、勉。娶夏氏。山東鄉試第十一名，會試第五十四名。
translation_en:
Song Qin 宋欽 (registered in a civilian household of Qian Subprefecture, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi; National University Student; specialized in the Classic of Changes [Yijing]; courtesy name Kejing 克敬; fourth in seniority; aged thirty-two, born on the sixteenth day of the first month). His great-grandfather was Song Bin 斌; his grandfather was Song Duan 端; his father was Song Ning 寧; and his mother was née Wang 王氏. Both of his parents are deceased. His elder brothers are Song Xuan 選 and Song Zun 遵. He married née Hou 侯氏. He placed eighth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Min 史敏 (registered in a military household of the Huai'an Guard in the Metropolitan Area [Zhili]; National University Student; specialized in the Record of Rites [Liji]; courtesy name Demin 德敏; second in seniority; aged thirty-one, born on the third day of the seventh month). His great-grandfather was Shi Wenhe 文和; his grandfather was Shi Guping 谷平; his father is Shi Jingyu 景餘; and his mother is née Xie 謝氏. Both of his parents are living. His elder brother is Shi Demao 德懋, and his younger brothers are Shi Dening 德寧 and Shi Deying 德英. He married née Pan 潘氏. He placed forty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefectural Examination and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Qian 張謙 (registered in a civilian household of Dangtu County, Taiping Prefecture in the Metropolitan Area [Zhili]; National University Student; specialized in the Classic of Poetry [Shijing]; courtesy name Mengqian 孟謙; third in seniority; aged forty-two [?], born on the first day of the twelfth month). His great-grandfather was Zhang Rong 榮; his grandfather was Zhang Junliang 均亮; his father was Zhang Fu 復; and his mother is née Chen 陳氏. His father is deceased and his mother is living. His elder brothers are Zhang An 安 and Zhang Xiang 祥. He married née Tang 湯氏. He placed seventy-sixth in the Yingtian Prefectural Examination and one hundred twenty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Run 高閏 (a military student registered in the Gaizhou Guard in Liaodong, originally from Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang; specialized in the Classic of Documents [Shujing]; courtesy name Juzheng 居正; fourth in seniority; aged twenty-nine, born on the thirteenth day of the intercalary fifth month). His great-grandfather was Gao Fuheng 復亨 (Department Magistrate of Xian Subprefecture under the Yuan); his grandfather was Gao Zongsi 宗泗; his father is Gao Guixiang 貴珦; and his mother is née Wang 王氏. Both of his parents are living. His elder brothers are Gao Jian 簡, Gao Jing 靖, and Gao Mo 黙; his younger brothers are Gao Ning 寧, Gao Shi 實, Gao Qin 勤, and Gao Mian 勉. He married née Xia 夏氏. He placed eleventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Tian Zhen 田瑧 (native of Xiangcheng County in Xuzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, registered in an artisan household; anAdded Student in the County School specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Zhidao; second in his generation; aged twenty-four, born on the thirteenth day of the sixth month). His great-grandfather was Zhongming; his grandfather was Rong; his father was Chun (Assistant Instructor in the Xuzhou School); and his mother is née Chen. His mother is living (his father is deceased). His elder brother is Xin. He married née Liang. He placed twenty-third in the Henan Provincial Examination and thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Yuan 馬垸 (native of Danyang County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Region [Zhili], registered in a commoner household; a County School Student specializing in the Classic of Documents (Shujing); courtesy name Bogu; third in his generation; aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-first day of the third month). His great-grandfather was Ren; his grandfather was Yi; his father was Zhi; and his mother was née Sun. Both of his parents are deceased. His elder brothers are Guangyi and Guang'er; his younger brothers are Guangsi and Guangwu. He married née Zheng. He placed seventy-fourth in the Yingtian Prefectural [Provincial] Examination and eighty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Jin 朱縉 (native of Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, registered in a commoner household; an Added Student in the County School specializing in the Record of Rites (Liji); courtesy name Tingyi; first in his generation; aged twenty-seven, born on the eighteenth day of the sixth month). His great-grandfather was Siwen; his grandfather is Nanyong; his father is Xiliang (Instructor in the Directorate of Education); and his mother is née Ma. Both his grandparents and parents are living. His younger brothers are Shen, Gang, and Ji. He married née Shao. He placed nineteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and one hundred sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhuang Min 莊敏 (native of Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, registered in a commoner household; a Prefectural School Student specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Tinggong; second in his generation; aged forty-one, born on the twelfth day of the tenth month). His great-grandfather was Shoufu; his grandfather was Run (posthumously honored as Secretary in the Ministry of Justice); his father was Qiancai (Assistant Administration Commissioner in the Huguang Provincial Administration Commission); and his mother was née Lin. Both of his parents are deceased. His elder brother is Yu (serving as Police Chief). He married née Lin. He placed eighteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and one hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Chang 王敞 (registered in an official household of Yongning Guard in Guizhou, a Confucian School Student of the Pacification Commission, specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals [Chunqiu]; style name Wenhao; fourth in seniority among his brothers; aged twenty-five, born on the fourteenth day of the fifth month). His great-grandfather was Wang Long (Associate Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs); his grandfather was Wang Xing (Judge); his father was Wang Bin; his legal mother is née Zhou, and his birth mother is née Yang. His mother is living while his father is deceased. His elder brothers are Wang Xuan (Judge), Wang Zheng, and Wang Min; his younger brothers are Wang Qi, Wang Zheng, Wang Shu, and Wang Jin. He married née Dai. He placed twelfth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and one hundred and tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Shushao 陳叔紹 (registered in a civilian household of Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, an Added Student of the prefectural school, specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals [Chunqiu]; style name Shushao; eighth in seniority among his brothers; aged forty, born on the seventeenth day of the third month). His great-grandfather was Chen Yao; his grandfather was Chen Yu; his father was Chen Zhou (invested with the title of Investigating Censor of the Sichuan Circuit), and his mother was née Lin (invested as Child Nurturer [ruren]). Both of his parents are deceased. His elder brothers are Chen Shugang (Academician Reader-in-waiting in the Hanlin Academy) and Chen Shumao; his younger brother is Chen Shufu. He married née Yang. He placed third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and ninety-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiang Jing 向敬 (registered in a civilian household of Zi County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, a county school student, specializing in the Record of Rites [Liji]; style name Xingjian; first in seniority among his brothers; aged thirty-five, born on the second day of the twelfth month). His great-grandfather was Xiang Wenyu; his grandfather was Xiang Bixian; his father is Xiang Fuzhong, and his mother is née Tan. Both of his parents are living. His younger brothers are Xiang Jian, Xiang Zheng, and Xiang Jin. He married née Deng. He placed thirty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chai Wenxian 柴文顯 (registered in a civilian household of Jiande County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, a prefectural school student, specializing in the Classic of History [Shujing]; style name Daoming; third in seniority among his brothers; aged forty-two, born on the eighth day of the fourth month). His great-grandfather was Chai Gui; his grandfather was Chai Zhongzhen; his father was Chai Yuanheng, his mother was née Wang, and his stepmother is née Wang. His mother (stepmother) is living while his father is deceased. His elder brothers are Chai Wenhao and Chai Wenzhi; his younger brothers are Chai Wenyi and Chai Wengui. He married née Qiu, and took a second wife née She… He placed thirty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Su Lin 蘇霖 (registered as a commoner of Longyan County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian; a County Student specializing in the Record of Rites [Liji]; courtesy name Kezi, third in seniority, aged thirty-six, born on the seventeenth day of the eleventh month). His great-grandfather was Guoyong, his grandfather Zhiyuan, his father Jishun, and his mother née Chen. With his mother living and his father deceased, he has elder brothers Keren and Kezhong, and younger brothers Kerong, Keli, Keshao, Mian, and Zui; he married née Wang. He placed twenty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Fang 董方 (registered as a commoner of Huo County, Shuntian Prefecture; a County Student specializing in the Classic of History [Shujing]; courtesy name Zhongju, first in seniority, aged thirty-eight, born on the seventh day of the eighth month). His great-grandfather was Youcai, his grandfather Xing, his father Zheng, and his mother née Zhang. With both parents living, he has a younger brother Zhi; he married née Zhang. He placed fifty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Shu 嚴樞 (registered as a commoner of Wan'an County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi; a National University Student specializing in the Classic of Changes [Yijing]; courtesy name Wuzheng, third in seniority, aged forty-four, born on the third day of the eighth month). His great-grandfather was Chengke, his grandfather Yuanheng, his father Zikuan, and his mother née Xiao. With both parents deceased, he has elder brothers Wugao and Wuli, and a younger brother Wujing; he married née Liu. He placed twentieth in the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination and ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao De 曹得 (registered as a commoner of Xiaoshan County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang; an Added County Student specializing in the Classic of Changes [Yijing]; courtesy name Xixian, first in seniority, aged forty-five, born on the eighteenth day of the eighth month). His great-grandfather was Shou, his grandfather Heng, his father Fo, and his mother née Zhu. With both parents deceased, he has a younger brother Wen; he married née Li. He placed thirty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and one hundred forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Yuxiang 劉羽翔 [native of Shan County 單縣, Yanzhou Prefecture 兗州府, Shandong, of commoner registration; prefectural student (fuxuesheng); specialized in the Classic of Rites (Liji); courtesy name Yuncheng 雲程; second in seniority among his brothers; aged thirty, born on the twenty-fourth day of the tenth month]. His great-grandfather was Tai 泰, his grandfather was Zheng 政, his father is Zhizhong 致中, and his mother is née Zhang 張. Both of his parents are living; he has an elder brother Fang 芳 and younger brothers Quan 泉 and Chong 翀, and is married to a woman née Wang 王. He placed seventeenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and one hundred twenty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

He placed twenty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and twenty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Lian 劉璉 [native of Daxing County 大興縣, Shuntian Prefecture 順天府, of commoner registration; added student of the prefectural school (fuxue zengguangsheng); specialized in the Classic of Documents (Shujing); courtesy name Zongqi 宗器; third in seniority among his brothers; aged twenty-five, born on the second day of the ninth month]. His great-grandfather was Da 達 [posthumously honored as Minister of Revenue (Hubu shangshu)], his grandfather was Zheng 正 [posthumously honored as Minister of Revenue], his father is Zhongfu 中敷 [Minister of Revenue], and his mother is née Liang 梁 [invested as Lady (furen)]. He placed sixty-seventh in the Shuntian Provincial Examination and sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Han 張翰 [registered in a civilian household of Anqiu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong; National University Student; specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Zongru; first in seniority among brothers; age forty-three, born on the fourth day of the third month]. Huang Shou 黃綬 [registered under a military household in Pinggu County 平谷縣, Shuntian Prefecture 順天府, Zhili 直隸; Student of the County School; specialized in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Wenxi 文璽; second in seniority among brothers; age forty-two, born on the twenty-ninth day of the seventh month]. His great-grandfather was Huang Jinqing 進卿; his grandfather was Huang Zhongli 仲禮 [Warden (siyu) in Yanzhou Prefecture 兖州府]; his father is Huang Yi 義; his mother was née Wang 王氏, and his stepmother was née Pan 潘氏. His father is living. His elder brother is Huang Jing 經, his younger brother is Huang Lun 綸, and he is married to née Zhang 張氏. He placed thirty-third in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and 131st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xiang 王瓖 [registered under a civilian household in Xiangcheng County 襄城縣, Xuzhou 許州, Kaifeng Prefecture 開封府, Henan 河南; Student of the County School; specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Zongxi 宗璽; third in seniority among brothers; age twenty-five, born on the twenty-third day of the fourth month]. His great-grandfather was Wang Decheng 德成; his grandfather is Wang Shangwen 尚文 [Right Assistant Administration Commissioner (you canyi) of Shaanxi 陝西]; his father is Wang Jingdao 警道; and his mother is née Yang 楊氏. Both his parents and grandparents are living. His elder brothers are Wang Zongqi 宗器 and Wang Zongzheng 宗正, his younger brother is Wang Zonggui 宗圭, and he is married to née Sheng 盛氏. He placed seventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 121st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao An 高安 [registered under a civilian household in Wei County 威縣, Guangping Prefecture 廣平府, Zhili 直隸; Added Student of the County School; specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Zining 子寧; first in seniority among brothers; age twenty-six, born on the ninth day of the tenth month]. His great-grandfather was Gao Wenli 文禮; his grandfather was Gao Qin 勤; his father is Gao Qing 清 [Instructor in the Medical School (yixue xunke) of this county]; and his mother is née Zhang 張氏. Both his parents are living. His younger brothers are Gao Xuan 宣, Gao Fu 富, Gao Bin 賓, and Gao Rong 容, and he is married to née Yang 楊氏. He placed twenty-second in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and 136th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Shen Ji 沈紀, courtesy name Wenzhen 文振, second in seniority among his brothers, aged twenty-eight, born on the eighteenth day of the twelfth month, was registered in an artisan household of Wanping County 宛平縣 in Shuntian Prefecture 順天府 and was a National University Student (guozi sheng) specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing). His great-grandfather was Shen Dexing 德興, his grandfather was Shen Shizhong 時中, his father was Shen Chongshan 崇善, and his mother was Lady Liang 梁氏; both his parents and grandparents were living. He had an elder brother, Shen Gang 綱, and was married to Lady Wu 吳氏. He placed fortieth in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Botong 潘伯通, courtesy name Xuegu 學古, second in seniority, aged fifty-three, born on the twenty-fourth day of the tenth month, was registered in a civilian household of Guangshan County 光山縣 in Guang Subprefecture 光州, Runing Prefecture 汝寧府, Henan 河南, and was an Added Student of the County School specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing). His great-grandfather was Pan Rong 榮, his grandfather was Pan Xiuxing 秀興, his father was Pan Daozhen 道真, his mother was Lady Shi 施氏, and his stepmothers were Lady She 佘氏 and Lady Zhang 張氏; his mother was living while his father had died. He had an elder brother, Pan Boliang 伯良, and a younger brother, Pan Bochang 伯昌, and was married to Lady Li 李氏. He placed one hundred and sixtieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and seventy-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Bao 戴珤, courtesy name Tingyong 廷用, second in seniority, aged twenty-seven, born on the eighth day of the ninth month, was registered in a military household of Hanshan County 含山縣 in He Subprefecture 和州 in the Metropolitan Area (Zhili 直隸), and was a County School Student specializing in the Classic of Documents (Shujing). His great-grandfather was Dai Sheng 勝, his grandfather was Dai Mian 冕, his father was Dai Zhongdao 中道, his principal mother was Lady Li 李氏, and his birth mother was Lady He 何氏; both his parents were living. He had an elder brother, Dai Tingyu 廷玉, and a younger brother, Dai Tingqi 廷器, and was married to Lady Wang 王氏. He placed seventy-second in the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination and one hundred and forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li He 李和, courtesy name Shizhong 時中, first in seniority, aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-sixth day of the seventh month, was registered in an artisan household of Qian'an County 遷安縣 in Yongping Prefecture 永平府 in the Metropolitan Area (Zhili 直隸), and was a Prefectural School Student specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing). His great-grandfather was Li Shanhou 善後, his grandfather was Li Bo'an 伯安, his father was Li Gui 貴, his principal mother was Lady Liu 劉氏, and his birth mother was Lady Zhang 張氏; both his parents were living. He had an elder brother, Li Tai 泰, and was married to Lady Wang 王氏. He placed ninety-sixth in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and eighty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Yao Shiliang 姚士良, his grandfather was Yao Yexun 姚埜遜, his father was Yao Li 姚禮, and his mother is née Qian 錢氏. His mother is living while his father is deceased. He has elder brothers Yao De 姚悳 and Yao Mao 姚懋, and he is betrothed to a woman née Gu 顧氏. He placed 30th in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 98th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zeng Zhuo 曾卓 [native of Yongfeng County 永豐縣, Ji'an Prefecture 吉安府, Jiangxi 江西; of commoner household registration; a County Student; specialized in the Record of Rites (Liji); courtesy name Yueyi 瀹沂; second in generational order; age thirty-seven, born on the fifteenth day of the eighth month]. His great-grandfather was Zeng Weizhao 曾惟昭, his grandfather was Zeng Wenqing 曾文清, his father is Zeng Deyong 曾德永, and his mother is née Peng 彭氏. Both of his parents are living. He has younger brothers Zeng Leyi 曾樂沂 and Zeng Guiyi 曾歸沂, and he is married to a woman née Li 李氏. He placed 10th in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 89th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Xuan 鄭瑄 [native of Jining Subprefecture 濟寧州, Yanzhou Prefecture 兖州府, Shandong 山東; of commoner household registration; a National University Student; specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu); courtesy name Tingxi 廷璽; second in generational order; age thirty, born on the second day of the third month]. His great-grandfather was Zheng Haoyi 鄭好義, his grandfather is Zheng Zhongwen 鄭仲文 [ Commandant of Music in the Confucian Temple (Kongmiao dianyue) ], his father is Zheng Xiuji 鄭脩己, and his mother is née Hao 郝氏. Both his grandparents and parents are living. He has an elder brother Zheng Qi 鄭玘 and a younger brother Zheng Jing 鄭璥, and he is married to a woman née Wang 王氏. He placed 4th in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 61st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Xuan 潘暄 [native of Jiading County 嘉定縣, Suzhou Prefecture 蘇州府, Southern Metropolitan Area (Zhili 直隸); of commoner household registration; a National University Student; specialized in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Shiyang 時陽; first in generational order; age thirty, born on the sixteenth day of the first month]. His great-grandfather was Pan Wenyi 潘聞誼, his grandfather is Pan Zhi 潘智, his father is Pan Tingyu 潘廷玉, and his mother is née Xia 夏氏. Both his grandparents and parents are living. He has a younger brother Pan Xu 潘昫, and he is married to a woman née Peng 彭氏. He placed 72nd in the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination and 46th in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 正統十年進士登科錄
text:
皇帝制曰自昔二帝三王致
理之道必選任賢才以敷
政化安中國而撫四夷其
見諸載籍靡不足為後世
法也下迨漢唐宋賢明之
===
君亦皆銳意於斯而其人
才治效有可以比隆於古
歟洪惟我
太祖高皇帝奉
天明命統一華夷

政化安中國而撫四夷其
見諸載籍靡不足爲後世
法也下迨漢唐宋賢明之
===
君亦皆鋭意於斯而其人
才治效有可以比隆於古
歟洪惟我
太祖高皇帝奉
天明命統一華夷

Coming down to the worthy and enlightened rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties, they too were all keenly intent upon this; yet among their men of talent and the results of their governance, were there any that could compare in splendor with antiquity? Humbly reflecting upon Our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu), he received the bright mandate of Heaven and unified Chinese and foreign peoples; …

text:
德威所被罔不臣服
太宗文皇帝嗣登大寶制治
保邦光前裕後

賢彙進教化旁洽海內乂
===

功德之盛脗合古昔而無
間矣朕纘承

translation_en: …wherever His virtue and majesty reached, there were none who did not submit as subjects. Emperor Wen, Taizong (the Yongle Emperor), succeeded in ascending the great throne; he established order and preserved the state, glorifying his predecessors and enriching his descendants. Successive Sacred Emperors inherited the throne one after another, all exalting the continuation and transmission of this legacy. The flourishing of their merit and virtue matched that of antiquity without the slightest gap. I have succeeded to the great enterprise; looking up in contemplation of the constant norms of My Ancestors, I take them as My instruction and put them into practice. I have repeatedly issued edicts to…

title: 正統十年進士登科錄
text:
中外簡拔賢才亦既得人
為用矣誠欲九德咸事野
無遺賢舉錯之法尚有可
行者乎申敕諸司修明治
理亦既建立事功矣誠欲
===
百工惟時庶績咸熙督勸
之典尚有可舉者乎内而
中國生齒之繁因其性而
教養之矣誠欲使皆𢌿厚
化成同歸於至治尚何所

translation_en: …at court and in the provinces to select and promote worthy talents, and we have indeed already obtained capable men for service; yet if we truly wish that those possessing the nine virtues all be employed and that no worthy be left neglected in the wilderness, are there still methods of promotion and dismissal that can be put into practice? I have repeatedly admonished the various offices to cultivate and clarify the principles of governance, and they have indeed already established meritorious achievements; yet if we truly wish that all officials act in timely fashion and that all their accomplishments flourish fully, are there still canons of supervision and encouragement that can be instituted? Internally, for the multitudinous population of the Central Realm, we have already educated and nourished them in accordance with their inherent nature; yet if we truly wish to cause them all to become honest and generous, with moral transformation brought to completion so that all return together to the perfection of governance, what more should be…

title: 正統十年進士登科錄
text:
加乎外而蠻貊近悅遠來
因其俗而懷撫之矣誠欲
使皆講信修睦相安於永
久尚何所施乎夫治道有
本而推行有序不法諸古
===
無以施於今泥於古而不
通於今亦不足以為治諸
生明於道藝必講之有素
悉著于篇朕將親覽焉

translation_en: … be added? Abroad, as for the southern and northern non-Chinese peoples, those nearby are pleased and those far away come in submission, and We have already cherished and pacified them in accordance with their customs; yet if We truly wish to cause them all to cultivate good faith and promote harmony, living together in peace forever, what further measures should be implemented? Now, the Way of governance has its root, and its implementation has its proper sequence. Without taking the ancients as a model, there is no means to put it into practice in the present; yet to cling rigidly to antiquity without adapting to the present is likewise insufficient to achieve good governance. You scholars are well versed in the Way and its arts, and have surely studied these matters thoroughly beforehand. Set forth everything fully in your essays, which We shall personally review.

title: 正統十年進士登科錄
text:
臣商輅
臣對臣聞圖治莫急於用賢用賢莫先於修身非
修身固無以為取人之本非用賢又無以為圖治
之要故中庸之書曰為政在人取人以身人君誠
能修身以為用賢之本用賢以為圖治之要則知
至意誠心正身修賢者在位能者在職以之亮天
工而熈庶績安中國而撫四夷何往而不得其效
哉欽惟
皇帝陛下聰明睿知文武聖神存二帝三王之心紹
祖宗列聖之統日
===
御經筵講求至道蚤晚
視朝裁决萬幾好賢之誠無間於話言圖治之切常
存於宵旰乃進臣等於
廷降賜
清問惓惓欲聞古今用賢致理之方所謂智周萬務
而不棄於一得之愚明照四方而必察於芻蕘之
賤是也
陛下是心與古帝王兢兢業業不自滿假用人惟巳望
道未見之心何以異哉臣雖愚昧敢不精白一心
以對揚

===
御經筵講求至道丞晚
視朝裁決萬幾好賢之誠無間於語言圖治之切常
存於宵旰乃進臣等於
廷降賜
清問惓惓欲聞古今用賢致理之方所謂智周萬務
而不棄於一得之愚明照四方而必察於芻蕘之
賤是也
陛下是心與古帝王兢兢業業不自滿假用人惟已望
道未見之心何以異哉臣雖愚昧敢不精白一心
以對揚
punctuated:
臣商輅。

臣對：臣聞圖治莫急於用賢，用賢莫先於修身。非修身固無以為取人之本，非用賢又無以為圖治之要。故《中庸》之書曰：「為政在人，取人以身。」人君誠能修身以為用賢之本，用賢以為圖治之要，則知至、意誠、心正、身修，賢者在位，能者在職，以之亮天工而熈庶績，安中國而撫四夷，何往而不得其效哉！

欽惟皇帝陛下，聰明睿知，文武聖神，存二帝、三王之心，紹祖宗列聖之統，日御經筵，講求至道，蚤晚視朝，裁决萬幾。好賢之誠無間於話言，圖治之切常存於宵旰，乃進臣等於廷，降賜清問，惓惓欲聞古今用賢致理之方。所謂「智周萬務而不棄於一得之愚，明照四方而必察於芻蕘之賤」是也。陛下是心，與古帝王兢兢業業、不自滿假、用人惟巳、望道未見之心，何以異哉！臣雖愚昧，敢不精白一心，以對揚…
translation_en:
Your servant Shang Lu 商輅.

Your servant replies: Your servant has heard that in seeking good governance nothing is more urgent than employing the worthy, and in employing the worthy nothing comes before cultivating one's own person. Without cultivating one's person, there is truly nothing to serve as the foundation for selecting men; and without employing the worthy, there is furthermore nothing to serve as the key to seeking good governance. Therefore, the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) says: "Government lies in men; men are selected by means of one's own person." If a ruler of men can truly cultivate his person as the foundation for employing the worthy, and employ the worthy as the key to seeking good governance, then knowledge will be extended to the utmost, intentions made sincere, the mind rectified, and the person cultivated; the worthy will be in positions of authority and the capable in offices. Using this to assist in the work of Heaven and make all achievements flourish, to pacify the Central Realm and soothe the four border peoples—wherever one turns, how could this fail to achieve its effect!

With reverent admiration I reflect that Your Majesty the Emperor is discerning, wise, and perspicacious, civil, martial, sagely, and divinely inspired. You preserve the mind of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, and continue the succession of the imperial ancestors and successive sages. Daily You attend the Classics Colloquium (jingyan) to investigate and seek the ultimate Way; morning and evening You hold court to decide a myriad of affairs. The sincerity of Your love for the worthy is unceasing in Your words, and the earnestness of Your pursuit of good governance is ever-present as You dress before dawn and eat late into the night. Thus You have brought Your servants forward into the court and graciously bestowed Your pure inquiry, earnestly wishing to hear the methods by which antiquity and the present have employed the worthy to achieve order. This is truly what is meant by "wisdom encompassing a myriad affairs yet not discarding the humble insight of a single success, and brilliance illuminating the four quarters yet invariably examining the lowly words of grass- and firewood-gatherers." How is this mind of Your Majesty any different from the mind of the ancient emperors and kings, who were cautious and trembling with care, never self-satisfied or arrogant, adopting the good of others as their own, and gazing toward the Way as though they had not yet seen it! Though Your servant is foolish and ignorant, how dare he not purify and devote his heart to respond to and extol…

title: 正統十年進士登科錄
text:
明命之萬一乎臣惟致治有要用賢是也用賢有本
修身是也若昔唐虞三代之世百姓昭明萬邦協
和而黎民有於變之風百工惟時庶績咸熙而萬
邦有咸寧之效二帝致治之隆如此者實本於其
登庸元愷不廢困窮之功也府事修和文命四敷
在商邑用協于厥邑在四方用丕式見德以至萬
民咸和丕單稱德三王致治之盛如此者亦本於
其籲俊尊帝克知克用之力也當是之時若臯夔
若稷契若伊尹周公各以賢聖之資居輔弼之任
或陳九德而諧八音或播百穀而敷五教一德足
===
以致天心之格成績足以篤烈考之光多士濟濟
布列庶位又豈無所自而然哉蓋由堯舜禹湯文
武之君或克明俊德而重華協帝或祗台德先而
聖敬日躋或緝熙敬止而無競維烈一皆本諸身
者無不誠見諸行者有其實所謂為政取人之方
著於載籍足以垂法於後世者何莫不自聖人修
身中来耶繼此而稱善治者莫漢唐宋若也其間
賢明之君未始不以用人為致治之本觀其孝廉
之有選賢良之有科或以明經進或以進士舉若
漢賈誼之勸興禮樂董仲舒之明於王道當時得

translation_en:
… one ten-thousandth of Your enlightened command!

Your servant reflects that bringing about good governance has an essential point, which is employing the worthy; and employing the worthy has a fundamental root, which is cultivating the self. In ancient times, during the eras of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, the hundred surnames were illustrious and enlightened, the myriad states were in harmony, and the black-haired people had the custom of transforming toward goodness; the hundred officials acted in accordance with the seasons, all achievements were resplendent, and the myriad states enjoyed the effect of universal peace. That the flourishing governance achieved by the Two Emperors was like this was truly rooted in their merit of elevating and employing the "Eight Worthies" (Yuankai) and not neglecting the distressed and impoverished. The six treasuries and three affairs were well-ordered and harmonized, and civilizing teachings were spread in all four directions; in the capital of Shang they brought harmony to their city, and in the four quarters they grandly served as models to manifest virtue; and at length the myriad people were all in harmony, grandly and wholly proclaiming their virtue. That the abundant governance achieved by the Three Kings was like this was likewise rooted in the strength of their calling upon men of eminence to honor the Supreme Ruler, and their being able to know them and to employ them.

At that time, men such as Gao Yao and Kui, Hou Ji and Xie, Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, each with the endowment of worthies and sages, occupied posts as輔弼 (assistant and counselor). Some set forth the Nine Virtues or harmonized the eight musical tones; some sowed the hundred grains or propagated the Five Teachings; some possessed single-minded virtue sufficient to move the heart of Heaven, or brought achievements to completion sufficient to consolidate the glory of their illustrious ancestors. That the multitude of Gentlemen, dignified and numerous, were arrayed throughout the various offices—how could this have come about without a source? It was because rulers such as Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu either were able to make bright their lofty virtue and match the Emperor in double splendor; or reverently took the cultivation of their own virtue first and saw their sage reverence daily ascend; or continued in bright and reverent attention to their resting point so that nothing could rival their illustrious merit. In every case, what was rooted in their own persons was never insincere, and what was manifested in their actions possessed true substance. As for what are called the methods of governing and selecting men recorded in the historical texts, sufficient to hand down as models for later generations—which of them did not come forth from the sages' cultivation of their own persons?

Following these, none were spoken of as having finer governance than Han, Tang, and Song. Among them, wise and enlightened rulers never failed to take the employment of men as the root of bringing about good governance. Observe how they had selections for the Filial and Incorrupt (xiaolian) and recruitment categories for the Worthy and Excellent (xianliang), or advanced men through the Classics Examination (mingjing), or recommended them as metropolitan graduates (jinshi). For instance, under the Han, Jia Yi urged the revival of rites and music, and Dong Zhongshu elucidated the Kingly Way; at that time…

title: 正統十年進士登科錄
text:
內富庶戎狄賓服其治效固有可稱者矣唐韓愈
之排斥佛老陸贄之論諫仁義當時中國乂安四
夷賓貢其治效亦有可觀者焉以至宋之韓范富
歐有以輔盛治於前周程張朱足以繼絕學於後
中國致文明之盛夷狄懷景仰之心其人才治效
雖不能比跡唐虞三代亦非漢唐所可及也雖然
漢唐宋之君其用賢圖治之意固云美矣而取人
以身之道則槩乎未有聞焉或詩書之妄事或禮
樂之未遑或閨門失德而治雜於夷或任用不專
而小人迭進外有尊賢之名內無用賢之實此漢
===
唐宋所以止於漢唐宋而不能儷美於唐虞三代
者亦以修身之道有未至也洪惟
聖朝
太祖
太宗以武功定天下以文德致太平
德澤溥施聲教遠被薄海內外莫不尊親際天極地
靡不臣服
