translation_en:
…the realm prosperous and populous within, and the western and northern tribes submitting as guests without—the effectiveness of their governance was indeed worthy of praise. In the Tang, there was Han Yu 韓愈 rejecting Buddhism and Daoism, and Lu Zhi 陸贄 discoursing and remonstrating on benevolence and righteousness; at that time the Central Lands were peaceful and secure, and the tribes of the four quarters came as guests bearing tribute—the effectiveness of their governance was also well worth beholding. Coming down to the Song, Han Qi 韓琦, Fan Zhongyan 范仲淹, Fu Bi 富弼, and Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩 were able to assist in a flourishing governance earlier on, while Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤, the Cheng brothers 程 (Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤), Zhang Zai 張載, and Zhu Xi 朱熹 sufficed to carry on the lost learning afterward. The Central Lands achieved the height of civilizing refinement, and the foreign tribes cherished feelings of admiration; although its talents and the effectiveness of its governance could not match the footsteps of Tang 唐 (Yao 堯), Yu 虞 (Shun 舜), and the Three Dynasties, neither could the Han and Tang reach them. Even so, while the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song certainly had admirable intentions in employing the worthy and planning for good governance, of the Way of selecting men by means of one's own personal conduct, practically nothing was heard. Some treated the Odes and Documents as a trifling matter [? 妄事, perhaps a misprint for 亡事 or 未事, "neglected the business of"], or had no leisure for rites and music; some lacked virtue in the inner quarters so that their governance was mixed with barbarian ways; some were not single-minded in their appointments so that petty men advanced in turn. Outwardly they had the name of honoring the worthy, but inwardly they lacked the reality of employing the worthy. The reason the Han, Tang, and Song remained merely the Han, Tang, and Song and could not rival the beauty of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties is also that they had not reached perfection in the Way of cultivating the person.
Greatly reflecting upon our Sacred Dynasty: Grand Progenitor (Taizu 太祖) and Grand Ancestor (Taizong 太宗) pacified All under Heaven through martial merit and brought about Great Peace through civil virtue. Their virtuous bounty was universally bestowed, and their prestige and teachings reached afar; within and beyond the four seas there were none who did not honor and love them, and to the ends of heaven and earth there were none who did not submit as subjects. Successive Sacred Emperors inherited the line one after another, gloriously opening up civil governance, exalting the Way of continuing and transmitting, and exhausting the methods of appointment and employment. 聖德神功盖昭合乎二帝三王之盛而漢唐宋之治
風斯下矣肆惟
皇上纘承鴻業遠稽帝王之道近守
祖宗之法孜孜以圖治為心惓惓以求賢為念其得人
致治之盛固已超軼乎古今矣而尤慮舉錯之法
未盡行督勸之典未盡舉內而教養未備外而撫
綏未至欲探其本而推行之以序臣愚以為是數

陛下之所已行行之而既效者也然尤欲求其本豈有

punctuated:
化成，夷狄傾心而內附。聖德神功，盖昭合乎二帝三王之盛，而漢、唐、宋之治，風斯下矣。肆惟皇上纘承鴻業，遠稽帝王之道，近守祖宗之法，孜孜以圖治為心，惓惓以求賢為念。其得人致治之盛，固已超軼乎古今矣；而尤慮舉錯之法未盡行，督勸之典未盡舉，內而教養未備，外而撫綏未至，欲探其本而推行之以序。臣愚以為，是數者皆陛下之所已行，行之而既效者也。然尤欲求其本，豈有外於陛下之修身乎？
陛下屢詔中外，簡拔賢才，其舉錯之法至矣；而尤欲求可行之法，臣願陛下謹修身以為舉錯之本，賢者必進而不肖者必退，如孔子所謂「舉直錯諸枉」，則「九德咸事」、「野無遺賢」之效不難致矣。陛下申敕諸司，脩明治理，其督勸之典備矣；而尤欲求可舉之典，臣願陛下謹修身以為督勸之原，勤者必賞而怠惰者必罰，
translation_en:
… transformed; and the foreign peoples incline their hearts in submission. Such sagely virtue and divine achievement clearly match the flourishing eras of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, whereas the governance of the Han, Tang, and Song falls far below them. Now Your Majesty has succeeded to the great enterprise, investigating the Way of the Emperors and Kings of antiquity while upholding the laws of the imperial ancestors in recent times, tirelessly setting Your mind on planning for good governance and earnestly fixing Your thoughts on seeking out the worthy. The flourishing of Your success in obtaining capable men and bringing about order has already surpassed both past and present. Yet You are still concerned that the methods of promotion and dismissal have not been fully put into practice, that the canons of supervision and encouragement have not been fully enacted, that within the realm instruction and nourishment are not yet complete, and that beyond the borders pacification is not yet thorough; and You wish to seek out their fundamental root and carry them out in proper sequence. In Your servant's humble opinion, all of these several matters are things that Your Majesty has already put into practice, and having practiced them, has already achieved results. Yet if You still wish to seek their root, how could it lie outside of Your Majesty's cultivation of Your own person?

Your Majesty has repeatedly issued edicts inside and outside the court to select and promote worthy talent, so Your methods of promotion and dismissal are already consummate; yet as You still wish to seek practicable methods, Your servant prays that Your Majesty will carefully cultivate Your own person as the root of promotion and dismissal, ensuring that the worthy are always advanced and the unworthy always dismissed, just as Confucius said, "Promote the upright and set aside the crooked." Then the results of "all men of the nine virtues serving in office" and "no worthy man left neglected in the wilderness" will not be difficult to achieve. Your Majesty has repeatedly admonished the various offices to clarify and cultivate the principles of governance, so Your canons of supervision and encouragement are already complete; yet as You still wish to seek canons that can be enacted, Your servant prays that Your Majesty will carefully cultivate Your own person as the source of supervision and encouragement, ensuring that the diligent are always rewarded and the indolent always punished, …

聖帝明王精神心術之所存仁義道德之所寓也
punctuated:
如《虞書》所謂「戒之用休，董之用威」，則百工惟時、庶績咸熈之效有可必矣。陛下既謹修身以為取人之本，將見人才之出彬彬乎盛。所以阜厚化成乎天下者，此也；所以講信修睦於夷狄者，亦此也。陛下嘗輕徭薄賦以立民命，建學立師以復民性矣。使凡任教養之責者，咸以利用厚生、教訓正俗為心，則人得以仰事俯育，而有尊君親上之心。生齒雖繁，有不同歸於至治乎？陛下嘗柔遠能邇以懷弗庭，厚往薄來以撫賓服矣。使凡典戎狄之職者，咸能諭之以禍福，示之以恩信，去者不追，至者不拒，訓兵練士，保境安民，則人畏威懷德，修貢稱藩。四夷雖遠，有不相安於永久乎？

夫為治之本在於用人，用人之本又在修身，必先其本而後其末。故《論語》曰：「君子務本，本立而道生。」《大學》曰：「身修而後家齊，家齊而後國治，國治而後天下平。」《中庸》曰：「知所以修身，則知所以治人，治天下國家。」皆此意也。雖然，修身固為用人之本，而欲用人致治，尤不可以不法諸古。蓋古者前代之法，聖帝明王精神心術之所存，仁義道德之所寓也。
translation_en:
… just as the Book of Yu (Yushu) says, "Admonish them with felicities, oversee them with awe," then the result that "all officials are timely in their duties and all achievements are resplendent" can be assured. Once Your Majesty carefully cultivates your person as the foundation for selecting men, we shall see men of talent emerge in flourishing abundance. That by which the empire is enriched and transformed through education is this; that by which good faith is cultivated and harmony maintained with the Yi and Di tribes is also this. Your Majesty has already lightened corvée labor and reduced taxes to establish the livelihood of the people, and built schools and appointed teachers to restore the moral nature of the people. If all who bear the responsibility of nourishing and educating take as their mind-set the promotion of useful conveniences, the enrichment of livelihoods, and instruction to rectify customs, then people will be able to serve their parents above and nurture their families below, and will possess the heart to honor their ruler and love their superiors. Though the population be numerous, how could they not all return together to the perfection of governance? Your Majesty has already been gracious to the distant and supportive of the near so as to win over those who do not attend court, and been generous in gifts sent out while expecting little in tribute returned so as to pacify those who have submitted. If all who hold office in charge of the Rong and Di tribes are able to instruct them regarding fortune and misfortune, display toward them grace and good faith, not pursuing those who depart and not rejecting those who come, training troops and drilling soldiers to protect the borders and give peace to the people, then men will stand in awe of your majesty and cherish your virtue, presenting tribute and declaring themselves vassals. Though the Four Barbarians (Siyi) be distant, how could they not remain in mutual peace forever?

Now, the foundation of governance lies in employing men, and the foundation of employing men lies in turn in cultivating the person; one must put the root first and the branches after. Thus the Analects (Lunyu) says: "The gentleman devotes himself to the root; when the root is established, the Way grows." The Great Learning (Daxue) says: "When the person is cultivated, the family is regulated; when the family is regulated, the state is rightly governed; when the state is rightly governed, the empire is made tranquil." The Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) says: "Knowing how to cultivate the person, one knows how to govern other men, and knows how to govern the empire, its states, and its families." All of these express this same meaning. Even so, while cultivating the person is indeed the foundation of employing men, if one wishes to employ men to bring about good governance, one especially cannot fail to model oneself upon antiquity. For the laws of former ages in antiquity are wherein the spirit and mind-craft of sage emperors and enlightened kings reside, and wherein benevolence, righteousness, morality, and virtue are lodged. …

punctuated:
傅說告高宗曰：「事不師古，以克永世，匪說攸聞。」使泥於古而或不通於今，則為徒法不能以自行矣。又必益之損之，與時宜之，《中庸》所謂「時措之宜」是也。
陛下之策臣者，臣既畧陳之矣，而於篇終竊有獻焉。臣惟始勤終怠者，衆人之常情；慎終如始者，聖人之要道。是故天地有常運而後歲功成，帝王有常德而後治功著。陛下德配天地，明同日月，誠又加夫不息之誠、有常之念，終始惟一，宵旰無間，則以之修身任賢，以之安民致治，遠足以追配二帝三王之道，近足以光昭祖宗四聖之業，上而致天地位，下而致萬物育，而綿曆數於無疆者，夫豈有越於此哉！臣干冒天威，不勝戰慄之至。臣謹對。
translation_en:
Fu Yue 傅說 told Gaozong 高宗: "That in handling affairs one could achieve perpetuity without taking antiquity as one's teacher is not something that I, Yue, have ever heard of." Yet if one clings rigidly to antiquity and fails to adapt to the present, then these become mere laws that cannot operate on their own. One must also add to them and subtract from them so as to suit the times—this is what the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong 中庸) calls "the appropriateness of timely application."

Regarding the policy questions Your Majesty has posed to Your servant, Your servant has already briefly set forth his views; yet at the close of this essay I venture to offer a further word. Your servant reflects that to be diligent at the beginning and lax at the end is the common inclination of ordinary people, whereas to be as careful at the end as at the beginning is the essential Way of the sage. Therefore, only when Heaven and Earth maintain their constant revolutions is the work of the year brought to completion; only when emperors and kings maintain their constant virtue is the achievement of good governance made manifest. Your Majesty's virtue matches Heaven and Earth, and Your brilliance equals the sun and the moon. If You truly add to this an unceasing sincerity and a constant mindfulness—remaining one and the same from beginning to end, without a moment's pause from before dawn until late at night—then by using this to cultivate Your person and employ the worthy, and by using this to bring peace to the people and achieve good governance, in relation to the distant past it will be sufficient to rival the Way of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, and in relation to the recent past it will be sufficient to gloriously illuminate the enterprise of our Imperial Ancestors, the Four Sages. Above, it will cause Heaven and Earth to find their proper places; below, it will cause the myriad things to be nourished; and as for extending the dynastic destiny without bound, how could anything go beyond this! Your servant has offended the Heavenly Majesty and is overcome with extreme trembling and awe. Your servant respectfully replies.

title: 正統十年進士登科錄
text:
臣周洪謨
臣對臣聞聖人之治本於道聖人之道本於誠
蓋誠者人心之實理誠以行道則心正身脩而
實體立道以出治則政善民安而實用著大哉
誠乎其萬事之樞紐萬化之本原乎二帝之所
以帝天下而克底雍熈者此誠也三王之所以
王天下而永臻康乂者此誠也我
國家
列聖所以創業垂統繼志述事而克享太平於永乆
者庸非此誠乎欽惟
===
皇帝陛下誕膺
駿命茂纘
鴻圖勤勵以親萬幾惇慎以弘萬化
純孝之德播聞於宇内仁厚之澤漸被於天下德巳
盛矣而猶懷懋德丕顯之心道巳至矣而常存望
道未見之念是以日
御經筵講求
聖學切劇治道臣有以知
陛下真大有為之君也乃又進臣等於
廷俯賜

臣周洪謨。

臣對：臣聞聖人之治本於道，聖人之道本於誠。蓋誠者，人心之實理。誠以行道，則心正身脩而實體立；道以出治，則政善民安而實用著。大哉誠乎！其萬事之樞紐、萬化之本原乎！二帝之所以帝天下而克底雍熈者，此誠也；三王之所以王天下而永臻康乂者，此誠也；我國家列聖所以創業垂統、繼志述事，而克享太平於永乆者，庸非此誠乎？欽惟皇帝陛下誕膺駿命，茂纘鴻圖，勤勵以親萬幾，惇慎以弘萬化。純孝之德播聞於宇内，仁厚之澤漸被於天下。德巳盛矣，而猶懷懋德丕顯之心；道巳至矣，而常存望道未見之念。是以日御經筵，講求聖學，切劇治道。臣有以知陛下真大有為之君也。乃又進臣等於廷，俯賜
translation_en:
Your servant Zhou Hongmo 周洪謨.

Your servant replies: Your servant has heard that the governance of the sages is rooted in the Way, and the Way of the sages is rooted in sincerity. For sincerity is the true principle of the human mind. When one acts upon the Way with sincerity, the mind is rectified, the person is cultivated, and the true substance is established; when one brings forth governance through the Way, administration is good, the people are at peace, and the true function is made manifest. Great indeed is sincerity! Is it not the pivot of the myriad affairs and the fountainhead of the myriad transformations? That by which the Two Emperors ruled All Under Heaven as emperors and were able to attain harmonious prosperity was this sincerity; that by which the Three Kings ruled All Under Heaven as kings and perpetually reached peace and order was this sincerity; and that by which the successive Sacred Emperors of our Dynasty founded the enterprise and handed down the tradition, carried on the intentions and continued the deeds of their predecessors, and were able to enjoy grand peace in perpetuity—was it not also through this sincerity?

Your servant reverently reflects that Your Majesty the Emperor has grandly received the Great Mandate and flourishingly succeeded to the vast enterprise, diligently attending in person to the myriad affairs of state and earnestly and prudently broadening the myriad transformations. Your virtue of pure filiality is proclaimed throughout the realm, and the grace of your benevolence and generosity gradually overspreads All Under Heaven. Your virtue is already abundant, yet you still cherish the mind to exert yourself in virtue so as to make it gloriously manifest; your Way is already at its utmost, yet you constantly preserve the thought of gazing toward the Way as though you had not yet seen it. Therefore, you daily attend the Classics Colloquium, investigating and seeking the learning of the sages and earnestly deliberating upon the Way of governance. Your servant thus knows that Your Majesty is truly a sovereign capable of great achievements. Now you have further advanced your servants to the court and graciously bestowed…

title: 正統十年進士登科錄
text:
清問而欲敷陳二帝三王致理之道推行之序臣愚
曷足以上揆
淵衷然敢不拜手稽首以對揚
聖天子之明命乎竊惟治非道不臻道非誠不立所謂
道者孰有外於脩身用人者乎稽之於古堯舜之
有天下不廢困窮舉任元凱內詢揆岳外咨牧伯
當是時也群哲勉輔由是典禮典樂掌刑掌教而
政化無不敷平治水土脩和府事而中國無不安
外薄四海咸建五長而四夷無不服探其本而論
之皆不越乎帝堯欽明文思帝舜温恭允塞之誠
===
而致然耳此二帝致理之道雖在得人而實本其
一心之誠之所致也禹湯文武之有天下忱恂九
德旁求俊彥克知三宅克用三俊當是時也群賢
既用由是不釐耿命脩和有夏而政化無不敷肇
域四海奄甸萬姓而中國無不安柔遠能邇重譯
来貢而四夷無不服推其原而論之皆不外乎禹
湯祗台德先懋敬厥德文武純亦不已克慎明德
之誠而致然耳此三王致理之道雖在得人而亦
本其一心之誠之所致也帝王之治道本於誠如
此其睿謨懿範載於四代之書者誠足以為帝王

punctuated:
清問，而欲敷陳二帝、三王致理之道、推行之序。臣愚曷足以上揆淵衷？然敢不拜手稽首以對揚聖天子之明命乎？

竊惟治非道不臻，道非誠不立。所謂道者，孰有外於脩身、用人者乎？稽之於古，堯、舜之有天下，不廢困窮，舉任元凱，內詢揆岳，外咨牧伯。當是時也，群哲勉輔，由是典禮、典樂、掌刑、掌教，而政化無不敷；平治水土，脩和府事，而中國無不安；外薄四海，咸建五長，而四夷無不服。探其本而論之，皆不越乎帝堯欽、明、文、思，帝舜温、恭、允、塞之誠而致然耳。此二帝致理之道，雖在得人，而實本其一心之誠之所致也。

禹、湯、文、武之有天下，忱恂九德，旁求俊彥，克知三宅，克用三俊。當是時也，群賢既用，由是不釐耿命，脩和有夏，而政化無不敷；肇域四海，奄甸萬姓，而中國無不安；柔遠能邇，重譯来貢，而四夷無不服。推其原而論之，皆不外乎禹、湯「祗台德先」、「懋敬厥德」，文、武「純亦不已」、「克慎明德」之誠而致然耳。此三王致理之道，雖在得人，而亦本其一心之誠之所致也。

帝王之治道本於誠如此，其睿謨懿範載於四代之書者，誠足以為帝王
translation_en:
…pure inquiry, wishing to have set forth the Way by which the Two Emperors and Three Kings achieved good order and the sequence for putting it into practice. How could your foolish servant be equal to fathoming the depths of Your Imperial mind? Yet how dare I not bow my hands and touch my head to the ground to respond to and extol the illustrious mandate of the Sacred Son of Heaven?

I humbly reflect that good governance cannot be attained without the Way, and the Way cannot be established without sincerity. As for what is called the Way, how could there be anything outside of cultivating the person and employing men? Examining antiquity, when Yao and Shun held All under Heaven, they did not neglect the distressed and impoverished, and they raised up and employed the "Eight Harmonies" and "Eight Worthies" (Yuankai); within the court they consulted the General Regulator and the Four Peaks, and in the provinces they took counsel with the Pastors and Leaders. At that time, the assembled wise men exerted themselves in assistance. Consequently, there were officials to direct the rites, direct music, take charge of punishments, and take charge of instruction, so that governance and moral transformation were everywhere diffused; the waters and land were brought to order and the six treasuries and three affairs were well-regulated and harmonized, so that the Central States were everywhere at peace; outward to the Four Seas, Leaders of Five States were everywhere established, so that the Four Yi tribes all submitted. If we probe the root of the matter and discuss it, all of this was simply brought about by nothing beyond the sincerity of Emperor Yao's being "reverent, intelligent, accomplished, and thoughtful" and Emperor Shun's being "mild, respectful, sincere, and thoroughly genuine." Thus, although the Way by which the Two Emperors achieved good order lay in obtaining the right men, in reality it was brought about by being rooted in the sincerity of their single mind.

When Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu held All under Heaven, they sincerely trusted those possessing the nine virtues, sought out men of excellence on all sides, were able to know those suited for the three high positions, and were able to employ those of the three abilities. At that time, once the assembled worthies were employed, consequently they grandly[?] ordered the bright mandate and well-regulated and harmonized the realm of Xia, so that governance and moral transformation were everywhere diffused; they bounded the territory within the Four Seas and broadly governed the myriad surnames, so that the Central States were everywhere at peace; they were gracious to the distant and supportive of the near, so that distant peoples came through repeated translations to present tribute, and the Four Yi tribes all submitted. If we trace the origin of the matter and discuss it, all of this was simply brought about by nothing outside of the sincerity of Yu's "paying reverent attention to my virtue first," Tang's "strenuously revering his virtue," and Wen and Wu's "purity that never ceases" and "being able to be careful of illustrious virtue." Thus, although the Way by which the Three Kings achieved good order lay in obtaining the right men, it too was brought about by being rooted in the sincerity of their single mind.

Such was the way the governance of the Emperors and Kings was rooted in sincerity; their wise counsels and admirable models recorded in the books of the Four Dynasties are truly sufficient to serve as the Emperors and Kings'…

title: 正統十年進士登科錄
text:
萬世之大法也自是而下漢則高帝之寬仁大度
文帝之恭儉玄默武帝之雄才大略光武之克復
舊物唐則太宗之聰明英武玄宗之勵精圖治憲
宗之剛明果斷亦皆銳意於斯者也然漢之諸君
意非不勤柰何不事詩書未免雜於伯道禮樂制
度又皆謙讓未遑奢欲既滋吏事深刻是皆不能
存此心之誠以為用賢圖治之本矣故語其人才
雖曰蕭曹賛畫平勃為相賈董才良鄧寇勳烈而
非皋夔之佐也語其治效雖曰黎民醇厚幾致刑
措西夷通道嶺南華風而非康衢之樂也漢之人
===
才治效如此比之唐虞三代何及哉唐之諸君志
非不勵柰何大綱不正慙德為多貞觀之治盛矣
而漸不克終開元之治美矣而弗能如始元和之
初威令復振逮夫晚年不終其業是皆不能盡此
心之誠以為用人致治之本矣故語其人才雖曰
玄齡善謀如晦善斷姚崇應變宋璟守正而非伊
傅之儔也語其治效雖曰斗米三錢外戶不閉窮
髮之地盡為編戶而非皇極之化也唐之人才治
效如斯較之唐虞三代則遠矣宋興太祖太宗之
創業真宗仁宗之守成亦皆追慕三代而景仰之

punctuated: 萬世之大法也。自是而下，漢則高帝之寬仁大度、文帝之恭儉玄默、武帝之雄才大略、光武之克復舊物；唐則太宗之聰明英武、玄宗之勵精圖治、憲宗之剛明果斷，亦皆銳意於斯者也。然漢之諸君，意非不勤，柰何不事《詩》、《書》，未免雜於伯道；禮樂制度，又皆謙讓未遑；奢欲既滋，吏事深刻，是皆不能存此心之誠，以為用賢圖治之本矣。故語其人才，雖曰蕭、曹賛畫，平、勃為相，賈、董才良，鄧、寇勳烈，而非皋、夔之佐也；語其治效，雖曰黎民醇厚，幾致刑措，西夷通道，嶺南華風，而非康衢之樂也。漢之人才、治效如此，比之唐、虞、三代，何及哉？唐之諸君，志非不勵，柰何大綱不正，慙德為多。貞觀之治盛矣，而漸不克終；開元之治美矣，而弗能如始；元和之初，威令復振，逮夫晚年，不終其業。是皆不能盡此心之誠，以為用人致治之本矣。故語其人才，雖曰玄齡善謀，如晦善斷，姚崇應變，宋璟守正，而非伊、傅之儔也；語其治效，雖曰斗米三錢，外戶不閉，窮髮之地，盡為編戶，而非皇極之化也。唐之人才、治效如斯，較之唐、虞、三代，則遠矣。宋興，太祖、太宗之創業，真宗、仁宗之守成，亦皆追慕三代而景仰之，
translation_en:
…the great model for ten thousand generations. From this time downward, in the Han there were Emperor Gao’s broad benevolence and magnanimity, Emperor Wen’s reverent frugality and profound quietude, Emperor Wu’s heroic talent and grand strategy, and Guangwu’s restoration of the old patrimony; in the Tang there were Taizong’s intelligence and martial prowess, Xuanzong’s vigorous commitment to good governance, and Xianzong’s firm clarity and decisiveness—all of whom also set their minds keenly upon this. Yet although the rulers of the Han were not lacking in diligence of intent, what could be done when they did not devote themselves to the Odes (Shi) and Documents (Shu), and inevitably mixed in the way of the hegemon (badao); when in rites, music, and institutional systems they politely declined as having no leisure for them; and when extravagant desires grew rife and administrative affairs became harsh and severe? In all these respects they were unable to preserve the sincerity of this mind as the foundation for employing the worthy and planning for good governance. Therefore, if one speaks of their men of talent—though it is said that Xiao He 蕭何 and Cao Can 曹參 assisted with counsels, Chen Ping 陳平 and Zhou Bo 周勃 served as Counsellors-in-Chief, Jia Yi 賈誼 and Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒 were of fine talent, and Deng Yu 鄧禹 and Kou Xun 寇恂 achieved illustrious merit—they were not assistants like Gao Yao 皋陶 and Kui 夔. If one speaks of the efficacy of their rule—though it is said that the common people were simple and honest, punishments were almost set aside, routes were opened to the western barbarians, and Chinese customs spread to Lingnan—it was not the joy of the highroads under Yao. Such were the men of talent and the efficacy of rule in the Han; compared with Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, how could they measure up?

As for the rulers of the Tang, their aspirations were not unroused, yet what could be done when the greatstays of morality were not upright and matters for shame in virtue were many? The governance of the Zhenguan reign (627–649) was flourishing indeed, yet gradually failed to be carried through to the end; the governance of the Kaiyuan reign (713–741) was admirable indeed, yet could not remain as it was at the beginning; at the start of the Yuanhe reign (806–820), imperial authority and ordinances were revived, yet by his late years the emperor did not bring his enterprise to completion. In all these respects they were unable to exhaust the sincerity of this mind as the foundation for employing men and bringing about good governance. Therefore, if one speaks of their men of talent—though it is said that Fang Xuanling 房玄齡 was skilled at planning, Du Ruhui 杜如晦 was skilled at deciding, Yao Chong 姚崇 adapted to changing circumstances, and Song Jing 宋璟 upheld rectitude—they were not the peers of Yi Yin 伊尹 and Fu Yue 傅說. If one speaks of the efficacy of their rule—though it is said that a peck of rice cost three cash, outer doors were not bolted, and the barren lands of the far north were all enrolled as registered households—it was not the transformation of the August Ultimate (huangji). Such were the men of talent and the efficacy of rule in the Tang; compared with Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, they fell far short.

When the Song arose, Taizu and Taizong in founding the dynasty, and Zhenzong and Renzong in conserving the achievement, all likewise looked back in longing to the Three Dynasties and revered them…

title: 正統十年進士登科錄
text:
是以當時真儒輩出治教休明人才治效可謂
庶幾三代矣然大綱雖正而萬目未盡舉要亦
由此心之誠有所未至耳是漢唐宋終不能比
隆唐虞三代者以其治之不能本於道道之不
能本於誠也洪惟
聖朝
太祖高皇帝奉
天明命奄有寰區以武功定天下以文德致太平
聖化所及無不忻戴
德威所被罔不賓服
===
太宗文皇帝嗣登大寶弘建兩京制治於既定保邦於
既安典章文物克光於前弘謨偉烈益裕於後
仁宗昭皇帝
宣宗章皇帝丕顯丕承善繼善述是以八十年間群賢
彙進無一才之不用教化旁洽無一所之不周海
宇之廣罔不乂寧四夷之遠悉皆賓服
神功聖德蓋與唐虞三代同一揆矣所以然者由乎
任賢才敷政化安中國撫四夷皆本於
列聖心純乎帝王之誠也
陛下以聖繼聖仰惟
alt_text:
是以當時真儒輩出治教休明人才治效可謂
庶幾三代矣然大綱雖正而萬目未盡舉要亦
由此心之誠有所未至耳是漢唐宋終不能比
隆唐虞三代者以其治之不能本於道道之不
能本於誠也洪惟
聖朝
太祖高皇帝奉
天明命奄有寰區以武功定天下以文德致太平
聖化所及無不忻戴
德威所被罔不賓服
===
太宗文皇帝嗣登大寶弘建兩京制治於既定保邦於
既安典章文物克光於前弘謨偉烈益裕於後
仁宗昭皇帝
宣宗章皇帝丕顯丕承善繼善述是以八十年間群賢
彙進無一才之不用教化旁洽無一所之不周海
宇之廣罔不乂寧四夷之遠悉皆賓服
神功聖德蓋與唐虞三代同一揆矣所以然者由乎
任賢才敷政化安中國撫四夷皆本於
列聖心純乎帝王之誠也
陛下以聖繼聖仰惟
punctuated:
是以當時真儒輩出，治教休明，人才、治效可謂庶幾三代矣。然大綱雖正，而萬目未盡舉，要亦由此心之誠有所未至耳。是漢、唐、宋終不能比隆唐、虞、三代者，以其治之不能本於道，道之不能本於誠也。

洪惟聖朝太祖高皇帝奉天明命，奄有寰區，以武功定天下，以文德致太平。聖化所及，無不忻戴；德威所被，罔不賓服。太宗文皇帝嗣登大寶，弘建兩京，制治於既定，保邦於既安，典章文物克光於前，弘謨偉烈益裕於後。仁宗昭皇帝、宣宗章皇帝丕顯丕承，善繼善述。是以八十年間，群賢彙進，無一才之不用；教化旁洽，無一所之不周；海宇之廣，罔不乂寧；四夷之遠，悉皆賓服。神功聖德，蓋與唐、虞、三代同一揆矣！所以然者，由乎任賢才、敷政化、安中國、撫四夷，皆本於列聖心純乎帝王之誠也。

陛下以聖繼聖，仰惟
translation_en:
…Therefore, at that time true Confucians emerged in great numbers, governance and moral instruction were splendid and enlightened, and the men of talent and the efficacy of rule could be said to have nearly approached those of the Three Dynasties. Yet although the great outlines were upright, the myriad details were not fully carried out; in sum, this too was simply because the sincerity of this mind had not yet been fully realized. Thus, the reason the Han, Tang, and Song could never equal the flourishing of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and the Three Dynasties is that their governance could not be rooted in the Way, and their Way could not be rooted in sincerity.

Vast indeed is our Sacred Dynasty! The Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu), received the bright Mandate of Heaven and came to possess the entire world, pacifying All under Heaven through martial merit and bringing about Great Peace through civil virtue. Wherever his sagely transformation reached, there were none who did not joyfully revere him; wherever his virtuous majesty extended, there were none who did not submit in allegiance. The Grand Ancestor, Emperor Wen (Taizong), succeeded in ascending to the Great Treasure, grandly established the two capitals, instituted order after stability had been achieved, and preserved the state after peace had been secured; his institutions, statutes, and cultural artifacts brought glory to what came before, while his grand plans and magnificent achievements further enriched posterity. The Benevolent Ancestor, Emperor Zhao (Renzong), and the Proclaiming Ancestor, Emperor Zhang (Xuanzong), grandly manifested and grandly continued the heritage, excelling in carrying on the intentions and undertakings of their predecessors. Therefore, over the course of eighty years, the multitude of worthies advanced together, with not a single talent left unused; moral instruction and transformation spread far and wide, with not a single place left unreached; throughout the vastness of the realm within the seas, there was nowhere not well-ordered and tranquil; and to the farthest reaches of the four quarters of non-Chinese peoples, all submitted in allegiance. Such divine achievements and sagely virtue indeed share the very same principles as those of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and the Three Dynasties! That it is so is because employing worthy talents, spreading governance and transformation, bringing peace to the Central States, and soothing the non-Chinese peoples of the four quarters have all been rooted in the successive reigning sages' minds being purely of the sincerity of the ancient Emperors and Kings.

Your Majesty, as a sage succeeding sages, looks up in reflection upon…

title: 正統十年進士登科錄
text:
祖宗之彜憲是訓是行是以屢詔中外簡拔登庸賢俊
在位庸劣遁跡舉錯之法可謂精矣尤欲求其可
行夫豈有他哉不過秉此心之誠以為舉直錯枉之
本則萬邦黎獻共惟帝臣而九德咸事野無遺賢
之效臻矣申勅諸司修明治理顯者已陟幽者已
黜督勸之典可謂至矣尤欲求其可舉又豈有他
哉不過秉此心之誠以為奨勤懲怠之本則內
外之臣皆懷激勸而百工惟時庶績咸熈之應至
矣內安中國因其性而教養之者已無一夫之不
獲尤欲使皆昇厚化成同歸於至治不過秉此心
===
之誠以為教養之本則至誠能化將見耕食鑿飲
向化敏德率為熈皞之歸矣外撫四夷因其俗而
懷撫之者已無一方之不服尤欲使皆講信脩睦
相安於永久不過秉此心之誠以為懷来之本則
至誠能感將見四夷左衽罔不咸賴率為中國之
氓矣夫治本於道道本於誠皆
陛下之所已行者也而又舉以策臣豈非
陛下體道謙冲不自滿假之誠之所發哉中庸論達道
達德九經皆曰所以行之者一也先儒謂一者誠
也

氓矣夫治本於道道本於誠皆
陛下之所已行者也而又舉以策臣豈非
陛下體道謙冲不自滿假之誠之所發哉中庸論達道
達德九經皆曰所以行之者一也先儒謂一者誠
也
punctuated: 祖宗之彜憲是訓是行。是以屢詔中外，簡拔登庸，賢俊在位，庸劣遁跡，舉錯之法可謂精矣。尤欲求其可行，夫豈有他哉？不過秉此心之誠，以為舉直錯枉之本，則萬邦黎獻共惟帝臣，而九德咸事、野無遺賢之效臻矣。申勅諸司，修明治理，顯者已陟，幽者已黜，督勸之典可謂至矣。尤欲求其可舉，又豈有他哉？不過秉此心之誠，以為奨勤懲怠之本，則內外之臣皆懷激勸，而百工惟時、庶績咸熈之應至矣。內安中國，因其性而教養之者，已無一夫之不獲。尤欲使皆昇厚化成，同歸於至治，不過秉此心之誠，以為教養之本，則至誠能化，將見耕食鑿飲，向化敏德，率為熈皞之歸矣。外撫四夷，因其俗而懷撫之者，已無一方之不服。尤欲使皆講信脩睦，相安於永久，不過秉此心之誠，以為懷来之本，則至誠能感，將見四夷左衽罔不咸賴，率為中國之氓矣。夫治本於道，道本於誠，皆陛下之所已行者也。而又舉以策臣，豈非陛下體道謙冲、不自滿假之誠之所發哉？《中庸》論達道、達德、九經，皆曰「所以行之者一也」。先儒謂「一者，誠也」。
translation_en: …the constant statutes of the Imperial Ancestors, taking them as your model and putting them into practice. Therefore, you have repeatedly issued edicts to the court and the provinces to select and promote men for office; the worthy and talented occupy positions while the mediocre and inferior have vanished from sight. Your method of promoting and setting aside men can truly be called refined. Yet you still wish to seek how it may be effectively practiced—how could this lie in anything else? It is simply a matter of holding fast to the sincerity of this mind as the foundation for promoting the upright and setting aside the crooked; then the multitudinous sages of the myriad states will all become subjects of the sovereign, and the efficacy of men of all nine virtues serving together with no worthy left neglected in the wilds will be achieved. You have repeatedly instructed the various offices to cultivate and clarify governance and administration; the illustrious have already been promoted and the obscure have already been demoted. Your canons of supervision and encouragement can truly be called utmost. Yet you still wish to seek how they may be fully implemented—how could this lie in anything else either? It is simply a matter of holding fast to the sincerity of this mind as the foundation for rewarding diligence and punishing negligence; then officials within and without the court will all feel inspired and encouraged, and the response of the hundred officials acting seasonably and all achievements being resplendent will arrive. Within, in bringing peace to the Central Realm, by educating and nourishing the people in accordance with their nature, there is already not a single person who has not found his proper place. Yet you still wish to make them all rise to generous customs and completed transformation, returning together to utmost governance. It is simply a matter of holding fast to the sincerity of this mind as the foundation for educating and nourishing; then, since utmost sincerity can transform, you will soon see them plowing for food and digging wells for drink, turning toward transformation and being earnest in virtue, all returning to a state of harmonious contentment. Without, in pacifying the four barbarians, by cherishing and soothing them in accordance with their customs, there is already not a single region that does not submit. Yet you still wish to make them all cultivate good faith and promote harmony, remaining at peace with one another in perpetuity. It is simply a matter of holding fast to the sincerity of this mind as the foundation for cherishing them and drawing them near; then, since utmost sincerity can move others, you will soon see the four barbarians who fasten their garments on the left all relying upon you without exception, all becoming subjects of the Central Realm. Now, governance is rooted in the Way, and the Way is rooted in sincerity—all of this Your Majesty has already put into practice. Yet you raise it further to question your servants in a policy essay: is this not an expression of Your Majesty's sincerity in embodying the Way with modest humility and refusing to be self-satisfied? When the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) discusses the universal ways, the universal virtues, and the nine standard rules, in every case it says: "That by which they are practiced is one." Former Confucians explained: "'One' means sincerity."…

title: 正統十年進士登科錄
text:
陛下全至誠之體於一心妙至誠之用於萬化以之奠
三才而育萬物以之六五帝而四三王所謂卓冠
群倫超越千古者端在於此矣治道之本
陛下固已立之若夫推行之序則中庸之九經曰脩身
尊賢親親敬大臣體群臣子庶民來百工柔遠人
懷諸侯大學之八條目曰格物致知誠意正心脩
身齊家治國平天下是其行之序也然所以行之
者又在
聖心之一誠耳誠以法帝王則考於古者皆合時措之
宜而不泥於古矣誠以法
===
祖宗則施於今者皆酌隆古之道而必宜於今矣誠乎
誠乎貫始終而無間者乎唐虞在位之久三代傳
祚之長皆誠以成始而成終者也漢唐諸君不能
誠以圖其始而保其終宋諸君則誠有未至者故
臣之對無他惟願
陛下常存此誠而已天至誠故常覆地至誠故常載
陛下常存此誠則博厚配地高明配天常厥德保厥位
而千萬世太平之洪業愈永而愈昌矣臣草茅
賤士學不足以上裨
聖治惟

punctuated: 陛下全至誠之體於一心，妙至誠之用於萬化，以之奠三才而育萬物，以之六五帝而四三王，所謂卓冠群倫、超越千古者，端在於此矣。治道之本，陛下固已立之；若夫推行之序，則《中庸》之九經曰脩身、尊賢、親親、敬大臣、體群臣、子庶民、來百工、柔遠人、懷諸侯，《大學》之八條目曰格物、致知、誠意、正心、脩身、齊家、治國、平天下，是其行之序也。然所以行之者，又在聖心之一誠耳。誠以法帝王，則考於古者皆合時措之宜，而不泥於古矣；誠以法祖宗，則施於今者皆酌隆古之道，而必宜於今矣。誠乎！誠乎！貫始終而無間者乎！唐、虞在位之久，三代傳祚之長，皆誠以成始而成終者也。漢、唐諸君不能誠以圖其始而保其終，宋諸君則誠有未至者。故臣之對無他，惟願陛下常存此誠而已。天至誠故常覆，地至誠故常載；陛下常存此誠，則博厚配地，高明配天，常厥德，保厥位，而千萬世太平之洪業愈永而愈昌矣。臣草茅賤士，學不足以上裨聖治，惟
translation_en: Your Majesty perfects the substance of utmost sincerity within your single mind, and manifests the wondrous function of utmost sincerity across the myriad transformations. Through it, you establish the Three Powers (Heaven, Earth, and Humanity) and nurture the myriad things; through it, you become the sixth alongside the Five Emperors and the fourth alongside the Three Kings. What is called towering above all peers and surpassing all antiquity truly lies in this. As for the foundation of the Way of governance, Your Majesty has assuredly already established it. As for the sequence of putting it into practice, the Nine Standard Rules in the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) are: cultivating one's person, honoring the worthy, being affectionate to relatives, respecting the great ministers, being empathetic toward the body of officials, treating the common people as one's children, attracting all classes of artisans, showing tenderness to men from afar, and cherishing the feudal lords; and the Eight Steps in the Great Learning (Daxue) are: investigating things, extending knowledge, making the intentions sincere, rectifying the mind, cultivating the person, regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to all under Heaven. Such is the sequence for practicing it. Yet that by which it is put into practice lies once again solely in the single sincerity of Your Sacred Mind. If through sincerity you model yourself on the Emperors and Kings of antiquity, then what you examine in antiquity will all accord with the appropriateness of timely application, without being bogged down in the past. If through sincerity you model yourself on the Imperial Ancestors, then what you implement in the present will all draw upon the Way of high antiquity, and will surely be suited to the present. Sincerity! Oh, sincerity! Is it not that which threads through beginning and end without interruption? The long reigns of Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun], and the enduring dynastic fortune of the Three Dynasties, were all cases of using sincerity to accomplish both the beginning and the end. The various rulers of the Han and Tang were unable through sincerity to plan their beginnings and preserve their ends, whereas with the various rulers of the Song, their sincerity was not yet fully realized. Therefore, your servant's reply has no other point: I only wish that Your Majesty will forever preserve this sincerity, and nothing more. Heaven is of utmost sincerity, and therefore forever shelters; Earth is of utmost sincerity, and therefore forever sustains. If Your Majesty forever preserves this sincerity, then in breadth and thickness you will match Earth, and in loftiness and brilliance you will match Heaven; you will make constant your virtue and preserve your throne, and the grand enterprise of Great Peace for ten thousand generations will grow ever more enduring and ever more prosperous. Your servant is a lowly scholar from the rustic wilds, whose learning is insufficient to aid Your Sacred Governance above; I only pray that…

title: 正統十年進士登科錄
text:
臣劉俊
臣對臣聞欲求為治之方不可不得其人欲知
得人之要不可不求諸巳蓋賢才乃立政之本
脩身實得人之要非賢才固不足以為治非脩
身亦不足以得人二帝所以官天下而躋世雍
熈者此也三王所以家天下而措世隆平者亦
此也漢唐宋之治效所以不能比隆於古者豈
非有外於此乎孔子曰為政在人取人以身非
無徵之空言也欽惟
皇帝陛下禀聰明睿智之資全聖神文武之德嗣承
===
大寶統御萬方尊賢使能俊傑在位賢已得矣
而尤以為未得教化旁洽世底雍熈治已至矣
而尤以為未至乃於萬幾之暇復進臣等于
廷降賜
清問首以二帝三王選賢圖治之實次及漢唐宋
人才治效之迹繼以我
朝
列聖得人致治之盛與夫
今日為政之本推行之序一言臣有以知
皇上之心即望道未見之心古六大有為之君也

臣劉俊。
臣對：臣聞欲求為治之方，不可不得其人；欲知得人之要，不可不求諸巳。蓋賢才乃立政之本，脩身實得人之要；非賢才固不足以為治，非脩身亦不足以得人。二帝所以官天下而躋世雍熈者，此也；三王所以家天下而措世隆平者，亦此也。漢、唐、宋之治效所以不能比隆於古者，豈非有外於此乎？孔子曰：「為政在人，取人以身。」非無徵之空言也。欽惟皇帝陛下，禀聰明睿智之資，全聖神文武之德，嗣承大寶，統御萬方，尊賢使能，俊傑在位，賢已得矣，而尤以為未得；教化旁洽，世底雍熈，治已至矣，而尤以為未至。乃於萬幾之暇，復進臣等于廷，降賜清問，首以二帝、三王選賢圖治之實，次及漢、唐、宋人才治效之迹，繼以我朝列聖得人致治之盛，與夫今日為政之本、推行之序一言。臣有以知皇上之心，即望道未見之心，古六大有為之君也。
translation_en:
Your servant Liu Jun 劉俊.

Your servant replies: Your servant has heard that if one wishes to seek the method of bringing about good governance, one cannot fail to obtain the right men; and if one wishes to know the essential way of obtaining the right men, one cannot fail to seek it within oneself. For worthy talents are the foundation of establishing governance, and cultivating one's own person is truly the essential way of obtaining the right men. Without worthy talents, it is certainly insufficient to bring about governance; without cultivating one's own person, it is likewise insufficient to obtain the right men. That by which the Two Emperors treated the realm as a public trust and raised the world to harmonious prosperity was this; that by which the Three Kings treated the realm as a family inheritance and placed the world in flourishing peace was also this. Could the reason that the achievements of governance in the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties failed to rival the splendor of antiquity be anything other than having departed from this? Confucius said: "Governance lies in getting the right men; getting the right men lies in cultivating one's own person." These are not unverified, empty words.

Reverently I reflect that Your Majesty the Emperor, endowed with the natural gifts of keen intelligence and profound wisdom, and complete in the virtues of sagehood, divinity, civil accomplishment, and martial vigor, has succeeded to the Great Treasure and rules over the myriad regions. Honoring the worthy and employing the capable, with men of outstanding talent in office, You have already obtained the worthy, and yet You still consider them not yet obtained; with moral transformation spreading far and wide and the world attaining harmonious prosperity, governance has already reached its height, and yet You still consider it not yet reached. Thus, in the leisure from a myriad affairs of state, You have again summoned Your servants to the court and graciously bestowed Your pure inquiry—first asking about the realities of how the Two Emperors and Three Kings selected the worthy and planned for governance; next touching upon the traces of talent and administrative effectiveness in the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties; continuing with the flourishing achievements of the successive Sage Emperors of our Dynasty in obtaining men and bringing about good governance; and concluding with a word on the foundation of governance today and the proper sequence for putting it into practice. From this Your servant has the means to know that Your Majesty's mind is none other than the mind that gazes toward the Way as though having not yet seen it—truly a sovereign of great enterprise like those of antiquity [? 古之大有為之君也, printed 古六大有為之君也]. …

賴賢才以共理之是賢才者為治之利器也稽
之於古唐虞之時以堯舜為之君則有皐夔稷
契為之臣斯時也州牧得人侯伯舉職刑罰清

萬邦有咸寧之效其所以然者何哉本於二帝
===
脩身得人以共治也三代之世以禹湯文武為
之君則有伊傅周召為之臣斯時也賢者在位
能者在職治道隆而風俗美四海平而天下安
人人有士君子之行比屋有可封之俗其所以
然者何哉本於三王脩身得人以共理也二帝
三王致理之道安中國而撫四夷者著於書寓
於易詠歌於詩皆足以為天下後世法也三代
而下得人之盛治效之隆莫漢唐宋若也漢之
七制唐之三宗宋之英君亦皆選任賢才以敷
政化安中國而撫四夷有志於二帝三王之治

國家生民太平之福，端在此矣。臣雖愚昧，敢不精白一心，以對揚□天子之休命乎？請因聖問所及而陳之。
臣聞天下之大，人君不能獨治，必賴賢才以共治之；庶務之繁，人君不能獨理，必賴賢才以共理之。是賢才者，為治之利器也。稽之於古，唐、虞之時，以堯、舜為之君，則有皐、夔、稷、契為之臣。斯時也，州牧得人，侯伯舉職，刑罰清而烝民粒，禮樂明而教化行，四方有風動之休，萬邦有咸寧之效。其所以然者何哉？本於二帝脩身得人，以共治也。三代之世，以禹、湯、文、武為之君，則有伊、傅、周、召為之臣。斯時也，賢者在位，能者在職，治道隆而風俗美，四海平而天下安，人人有士君子之行，比屋有可封之俗。其所以然者何哉？本於三王脩身得人，以共理也。二帝、三王致理之道，安中國而撫四夷者，著於《書》，寓於《易》，詠歌於《詩》，皆足以為天下後世法也。
三代而下，得人之盛，治效之隆，莫漢、唐、宋若也。漢之七制、唐之三宗、宋之英君，亦皆選任賢才，以敷政化，安中國而撫四夷，有志於二帝、三王之治
translation_en:
The blessing of great peace for the state and the people truly lies right here. Though your servant is foolish and ignorant, how could he dare not purify his heart in single-minded devotion to respond to and extol the beneficent charge of the [?] Son of Heaven? Allow me to set forth my views following what Your Sacred Inquiry has touched upon.
Your servant has heard that the empire is so vast that a ruler cannot govern it alone, and must rely on worthy talents to govern it together with him; the myriad affairs of state are so numerous that a ruler cannot manage them alone, and must rely on worthy talents to manage them together with him. Thus, worthy talents are the sharp instruments of governance. Examining antiquity, in the eras of Tang and Yu, when Yao and Shun were the rulers, they had Gao Yao, Kui, Hou Ji, and Xie as their ministers. At that time, the Pastors of the Provinces were the right men, and the marquises and earls fulfilled their duties; punishments were clear and the multitude of the people had grain to eat; rites and music were illustrious and moral transformation prevailed; the four quarters enjoyed the grace of being moved as if by the wind, and the myriad states experienced the effect of universal tranquility. Why was this so? It was rooted in the Two Emperors cultivating their persons and obtaining the right men to govern together with them. In the age of the Three Dynasties, when Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu were the rulers, they had Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao as their ministers. At that time, the worthy held positions and the capable held office; the way of governance flourished and customs were admirable; the four seas were pacified and the empire was at peace; everyone had the conduct of a gentleman, and every household side by side had customs worthy of enfeoffment. Why was this so? It was rooted in the Three Kings cultivating their persons and obtaining the right men to manage together with them. The Way by which the Two Emperors and Three Kings achieved good order, bringing peace to the Central States and pacifying the four border tribes, is set forth in the Book of Documents (Shu), embodied in the Book of Changes (Yi), and sung of in the Book of Odes (Shi); all of these suffice to serve as a model for the empire and later generations.
From the Three Dynasties downward, in the abundance of men obtained and the flourishing of the results of governance, none equaled the Han, Tang, and Song. The seven rulers of the Han who established institutions, the three illustrious ancestors of the Tang, and the heroic rulers of the Song likewise all selected and appointed worthy talents in order to spread administrative transformation, bring peace to the Central States, and pacify the four border tribes; they were rulers who aspired to the governance of the Two Emperors and Three Kings…

translation_en:
…[who aspired to the governance of the Two Emperors and Three Kings]. In the Han there were Xiao [He 蕭何], Cao [Can 曹參], Bing [Ji 丙吉], and Wei [Xiang 魏相]; in the Tang there were Fang [Xuanling 房玄齡], Du [Ruhui 杜如晦], Yao [Chong 姚崇], and Song [Jing 宋璟]; in the Song there were Han [Qi 韓琦], Fan [Zhongyan 范仲淹], Fu [Bi 富弼], and Ouyang [Xiu 歐陽脩]. Yet although the worthies and talents of the Han, Tang, and Song had merits worth praising, compared to those of the eras of Tang [Yao], Yu [Shun], and the Three Dynasties, they fell far short indeed. For this reason, in nourishing the people they could only attain lesser tranquility (xiaokang), and could not cause them to eat their fill and drum their bellies in contentment, fulfilling their natural dispositions like kites flying in the sky and fishes leaping in the deep; in instructing the people they could only bring them to understand righteousness, and could not cause them to move toward goodness and be diligent in virtue, being molded by an imperceptible transformation in which they knew not how it came about. Why is it that the talents and administrative efficacy of the Han, Tang, and Song could not rival the splendor of antiquity? Precisely because those who were rulers could not personally practice the virtue of the mind as the essential basis for selecting men, and those who were ministers could not assist their rulers in attaining utmost benevolence as the fundamental root of governing the people.

Humbly reflecting upon our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu Gao Huangdi, r. 1368–1398): he received the bright Mandate of Heaven, unified Chinese and barbarians, founded the dynastic enterprise and handed down the succession, opening up ten thousand generations of Great Peace; wherever his moral virtue and martial awe reached, the barbarian tribes submitted in allegiance. The Grand Ancestor, Emperor Wen (Taizong Wen Huangdi, r. 1402–1424), succeeded to the precious throne, continuing the line and preserving the accomplishments, regulating governance and securing the state, glorifying his predecessors and enriching his posterity. The Benevolent Ancestor, Emperor Zhao (Renzong Zhao Huangdi, r. 1424–1425), and the Proclaiming Ancestor, Emperor Zhang (Xuanzong Zhang Huangdi, r. 1425–1435)—this succession of sacred emperors carried on the heritage, earnestly honoring the ancient Way. Therefore, worthy men advanced together in multitudes, moral teaching and transformation spread far and wide, the Four Seas were well-ordered and peaceful, and the myriad regions looked up in grateful allegiance—harmoniously enclosed within the realm of the Spring Terrace and the Jade Candle of seasonable harmony, and serenely resting beneath [□□; under the auspices of?] auspicious stars and felicitous clouds. The flourishing of their meritorious virtue and the height of their administrative efficacy match those of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties without the slightest gap,…

punctuated: 異世而同符矣。所以然者，蓋由列聖脩身、得人以致之也。欽惟皇帝陛下嗣登寶位，纘承鴻業，體堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之心以為心，法祖宗列聖為治之道以為治。屢詔中外簡拔賢才，内而左右輔弼者，皆藹藹之吉人；外而承流宣化者，咸濟濟之賢士。亦既得人為用矣，陛下尤以舉錯之法詢臣。臣以為選任之際，所舉者果直，所錯者果枉，則賢者進而不肖者退，「九德咸事」、「野無遺賢」之效，豈有不得者乎？申敕諸司修明治理，小大之臣各敬其事，内外之官無曠其職。亦既建立事功矣，陛下尤以督勸之典詢臣。臣以為考課之際，所陟者果明，所黜者果幽，則勤者勸而惰者懲，「百工惟時」、「庶績咸熈」之驗，豈有不著者乎？内而中國生齒之繁，既制田里以厚其生，設學校以明其性，所以教養之者備矣。陛下尤欲使之曶厚化成，同歸於至治。臣以為在於申明教化之有其方，勸課農桑之有其實，則不患其效之不著。外而蠻貊近悦遠來，既撫之以
translation_en:
…though in different eras, tally as one. The reason this is so is surely that the Successive Sacred Emperors brought it about by cultivating their persons and obtaining worthy men.

Reverently I reflect that Your Majesty the Emperor has succeeded to the Precious Throne and inherited the Great Enterprise, embodying the minds of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu as Your own mind, and modeling Your governance upon the way of governance of the Imperial Ancestors and Successive Sacred Emperors. You have repeatedly issued edicts to the court and the provinces to select and promote worthy talents. Within the court, those who assist and counsel at Your left and right are all admirable good men in abundance; outside in the provinces, those who transmit the sovereign's grace and spread moral transformation are all numerous worthy gentlemen. Thus You have already obtained men for service, yet Your Majesty still questions Your servant regarding the methods of promotion and dismissal. Your servant holds that at the time of selection and appointment, if those promoted are truly upright and those set aside are truly crooked, then the worthy will advance and the unworthy will retreat—how could the effects of "all who possess the nine virtues being in service" and "no worthy men being left overlooked in the wilderness" fail to be attained?

You have repeatedly admonished the various offices to cultivate and clarify governance and administration, so that officials great and small each reverence their duties, and officers inside and outside the capital do not neglect their posts. Thus achievements in governance have already been established, yet Your Majesty still questions Your servant regarding the statutes for supervision and encouragement. Your servant holds that at the time of performance evaluation, if those promoted are truly the enlightened and those demoted are truly the benighted, then the diligent will be encouraged and the indolent punished—how could the proof of "all officials acting in accordance with the seasons" and "all achievements being resplendent" fail to become manifest?

Within, as for the burgeoning population of the Central Realm, You have already regulated fields and villages to enrich their livelihood, and established schools to illuminate their innate nature; the means of educating and nourishing them are complete. Yet Your Majesty still wishes to render their customs generous [?] and their moral transformation complete, so that all return together to the utmost order. Your servant holds that this lies in having proper methods for clarifying and proclaiming moral instruction, and having genuine substance in encouraging and supervising agriculture and sericulture; then there will be no need to worry that these effects will fail to become manifest.

Without, as for the barbarian tribes, those near rejoice and those far away come in submission; You have already soothed them with…

title: 正統十年進士登科錄
text:
仁待之以禮所以懷柔之者至矣
陛下尤欲使之講信修睦相安於永久臣以為在以
厚往薄來懷之以恩信不寶遠物置之於度外
則不患其效之不臻然以臣其原而論之皆不過
修身用賢二者而已大抵為治之道以賢才為
本推行之序以修身為先能修其身則不患賢
才之不得既得賢才則不患天下之不治故中
庸以尊賢居修身之次大學以修身為齊家治
國平天下之本也雖然為治固有其本推行固
有其序然又不可以不法諸古也蓋古者今之
===
所當法也為治而能法諸古則用力少而成功
多故孟子曰為高必因丘陵為下必因川澤為
政不因先王之道可謂智乎
陛下誠能修身以取人酌古以準今上不違先王之
道下不失時措之宜如是人以之安中國則中國
乂寧以之撫四夷則四夷賓服天地以之而位
萬物以之而育為生民立命為萬世開太平無
所施不可矣臣學術膚淺不足以奉
大對謹竭愚陋以獻惟
皇上採擇焉臣不勝戰懼之至臣謹對

punctuated: 仁，待之以禮，所以懷柔之者至矣。陛下尤欲使之講信修睦，相安於永久。臣以為在以厚往薄來，懷之以恩信；不寶遠物，置之於度外，則不患其效之不臻。然以臣其原而論之，皆不過修身、用賢二者而已。大抵為治之道，以賢才為本；推行之序，以修身為先。能修其身，則不患賢才之不得；既得賢才，則不患天下之不治。故《中庸》以尊賢居修身之次，《大學》以修身為齊家、治國、平天下之本也。雖然，為治固有其本，推行固有其序，然又不可以不法諸古也。蓋古者，今之所當法也。為治而能法諸古，則用力少而成功多。故《孟子》曰：「為高必因丘陵，為下必因川澤。為政不因先王之道，可謂智乎？」陛下誠能修身以取人，酌古以準今，上不違先王之道，下不失時措之宜，如是人以之安中國，則中國乂寧；以之撫四夷，則四夷賓服；天地以之而位，萬物以之而育，為生民立命，為萬世開太平，無所施不可矣。臣學術膚淺，不足以奉大對，謹竭愚陋以獻，惟皇上採擇焉。臣不勝戰懼之至，臣謹對。
translation_en:
… benevolence and treating them with ritual propriety, the means of winning them over and pacifying them have reached the utmost. Yet Your Majesty still wishes to cause them to cultivate trustworthiness and maintain harmony, abiding in mutual peace forever. Your servant considers that this lies in giving generously to those who depart and accepting little from those who come, winning them over with grace and good faith, and not prizing goods from afar, leaving them outside your concern; then one need not worry that such effects will not be attained.

Yet if your servant traces [?] their source and discusses them, all of these come down to nothing more than two things: cultivating the person and employing the worthy. On the whole, in the Way of governance, worthy talents are the root; in the sequence of putting it into practice, cultivating the person comes first. If one can cultivate one's person, there is no need to worry that worthy talents will not be obtained; once worthy talents are obtained, there is no need to worry that the realm will not be well governed. Therefore, the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) places honoring the worthy right after cultivating the person, and the Great Learning (Daxue) takes cultivating the person as the root of regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the realm.

Even so, while governance certainly has its root and its implementation certainly has its sequence, one also cannot fail to take the ancients as a model. For antiquity is what the present ought to model itself upon. If in governing one is able to model oneself upon the ancients, the effort expended is small while the achievement is great. Thus the Mencius (Mengzi) says: "To raise something high, one must make use of hills and mounds; to excavate something low, one must make use of streams and marshes. If in conducting government one does not make use of the Way of the Former Kings, can one be called wise?"

If Your Majesty can truly cultivate your person in order to select men, and deliberate upon antiquity in order to set standards for the present—above, not violating the Way of the Former Kings, and below, not losing the appropriateness of timely measures—then [?], used to bring peace to the Central States, the Central States will be tranquil and well-ordered; used to pacify the four border peoples, the four border peoples will submit in allegiance; Heaven and Earth will thereby find their proper places, the myriad things will thereby be nourished, a destiny will be established for the living people, and great peace will be opened up for ten thousand generations—there will be nothing to which it cannot be applied!

Your servant's learning is shallow and superficial, insufficient to offer a grand reply. I respectfully exhaust my foolish and humble thoughts to present them, praying only that the August Emperor may select from them. Your servant is overcome with the utmost trembling and fear. Your servant respectfully replies.
